#1908. Xabi Alonso takes aim at his Chelsea players after shock Sunderland defeat

Xabi Alonso was not looking for excuses after his Chelsea side was beaten 1-0 at Sunderland, admitting they did not defend or attack well enough.

The Black Cats were bottom of the Premier League table with just one win in nine games when they welcomed Chelsea to the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon.

The Blues returned to London with nothing, though, with an Enzo Le Fee penalty the difference between the sides.

There was controversy over the penalty decision, with Levi Colwill adjudged to have hauled down Brian Brobbey, although it looked like both players were pulling the shirt of the other.

Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders hit out at the decision, telling Sky Sports: ‘For me it wasn’t a penalty. He barely touched him, I think it was the other way round. He grabbed him.’

Alonso was not singing from the same hymn sheet, telling the BBC: ‘I haven’t seen it back. Nothing to comment on the referee. It is something that is our fault. We could have done better.’

He added: ‘I think it’s an action where he can defend better. It’s our mistake.’

Alonso was impressed by Brobbey over the game, not just in winning the penalty, but felt his defenders could have done better against the big Dutchman.

‘From transitions out of almost nothing he got a couple of chances, he got the penalty as well,’ he said. ‘But we have been preparing for that, we have tried, we could have done better.

‘He is not unstoppable. He is stoppable but when you defend better than we did today.’

‘We were against a low block we missed a bit of patience, a bit of quality, a bit of creativity on the last third to create more chances, you need to be more consistent to move the ball from one side to the other that we didn’t do good enough.’

It was suggested to Alonso that Sunderland’s physical superiority meant they could bully Chelsea, but the manager said: ‘Not bullied. There’s situations that we could have defended better. Situations that we could have had better advantages in attack.’

Defeat left Chelsea fifth in the table, while Sunderland climbed to 18th.

#1905. As I sat in the Sir Alex Ferguson Stand, the raw emotion and magic of Old Trafford was all around me. It was a stark reminder that the fans and the place they flock to really are Man United's greatest gift, writes IAN HERBERT

Published: 07:00 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 06:22 EST, 5 November 2026

The sound came rolling down in waves, crashing down around us as I sat in the Sir Alex Ferguson Stand, in the moments after Manchester United had conceded a most dreadful first goal. It was low and sonorous and quite extraordinary, really.

When a club go nine games without winning and fall behind again, you expect an air of sullen resignation – not that ‘UNITED’ which took hold and grew in a collective, magical act of defiance.

Much more would follow in a significant escalation of protest against the Glazers and their minority partner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. But in that moment – and once more when Roma’s second goal threatened to turn this into a catastrophe – it was just about the terraces and their team. A fanbase refusing to go gently into a night of quiet desperation.

Much has been made of the supposed need to let go of a history which has weighed heavy on this club since Sir Alex stepped away. In turn, United try to release it and then cleave to it again, blindly staggering around in their wilderness.

But on Tuesday night, in the stand bearing the great manager’s name, you looked around and were reminded of how the folk memory of Law, Best, Charlton, Cantona and Rooney is such a powerful weapon. It binds the fans back to what was once great. It is fuel.

What those fans brought into the stadium was not a naive and nostalgic sentimentality. They still demanded the best of the players. There is a clear acceptance among many that Bruno Fernandes is trying to repair things, but when he went down theatrically and protested about a challenge, he was told, ‘stop whinging’.

Michael Carrick celebrates Manchester United's victory over Roma on an incredible Old Trafford Champions League night

Matheus Cunha reacts after scoring United's third goal in their comeback win

This is a discerning, intelligent football public. ‘Standards’ is the word on that banner that’s been flying on the Stretford End.

But the collective view before kick-off was that if the players gave fully, then the fans were with them. ‘I just need to know they’re trying,’ said my friend Jocelyn, as we threaded our way through the crowds to the stadium.

Harry Maguire, who has lived this period of United struggle in the raw and was terribly exposed in a wretched first half, still wore that perpetual look of defiance on his face. When United were fatefully awarded the retaken penalty kick, some were saying that Maguire should be handed the ball. ‘At least he’ll put his foot through it.’

There was a frustration with the way that moments of promise broke down, as passes from Kobbie Mainoo and Carlos Baleba went astray. And with the time it takes Senne Lammens to decide how to distribute the ball, which slows United dreadfully. Yet a recognition of the fight shown by individuals who were patently playing for and engaging with the struggles of Carrick, while contending with a scorching scrutiny.

The shadow on the wall was the owners, of course. It was significant that the chants of derision for them struck up on the Stretford End each time United scored. As if to say that the green and gold campaign won’t fade with the slightest prospect of hope this time. There were tennis balls, balloons and a sense that something is building.

Even now, after 21 years, do the Glazers, hiding in their Florida redoubt, really know that they are playing with fire? This now feels as visceral as Liverpool fans’ hate for Tom Hicks and George Gillett Jnr, 20 years ago.

That club’s fans found ways of getting them out. They email-bombed every outfit that seemed ready to offer to help them, from Royal Bank of Scotland to US equity firm Blackstone. The audible boos when the tennis balls rained down after 20 minutes and five seconds – 20.05 represents the year the Glazers staged their leveraged buy-out – suggests protests affecting play are unwelcome for some and perhaps many. Yet the fury is unbridled. The centre may not hold this time.

The night, however, was about the power of this place to do extraordinary things. Even when Bryan Mbeumo crashed a golden chance to equalise against the post in the early stages of the comeback, you sensed something was afoot.

You’re so close to the pitch in the lower tiers of the Sir Alex Ferguson Stand that you feel you can almost reach out and touch the players. As the stadium gave, so they received. Fernandes marshalled. Youri Tielemans made a difference. Matheus Cunha seized the game by the throat.

Cunha and Shea Lacey race towards the jubilant crowd after United's third goal

And suddenly, like a river, that anthem was taking hold. ‘It’s Carrick you know. It’s hard to believe it’s not Scholes’ – over and over again

And suddenly, like a river, that anthem was taking hold. ‘It’s Carrick you know. It’s hard to believe it’s not Scholes’ – over and over again. At the end Diego Dalot was flat out on his back before us. Mason Mount, who’d been on the field barely five minutes, was in delirium and the post-match acknowledgement of fans by Carrick with his players felt like a victory lap. It meant that much.

The Carrick anthem was still being sung on the concourses as we flooded out under the clear night sky, and you knew for sure in that moment why no one wants the distinctly average names like Eddie Howe, Unai Emery and Julian Nagelsmann being touted for this job.

‘I don’t want us to start all over again,’ Jocelyn told me, still trying to compute what we’d just seen, after we'd joined the departing throng. ‘I want Carrick to do it. I want more nights like this.’

We learned in the aftermath that Carrick’s career-saving half-time speech had involved him telling his players how Old Trafford could do this. ‘I don't like to keep talking to the lads about what this place can do and the history and what's gone before too much, but it's there,’ he said. ‘This place does magical things. It's done it before and it'll do it over and over again.’

Yes, that really did encapsulate the essence of a night on which we discovered, once more, that the fans and the place they flock to really are Manchester United's greatest gift.

#1903. Michael Carrick responds to Man Utd relegation fears after Aston Villa draw

Michael Carrick downplayed fears Manchester United were in a relegation battle after a remarkable 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

United will sit in the relegation zone of the Premier League during the November international break after a thrilling 4-4 draw with Villa at Old Trafford.

Aston Villa twice led by two goals but Manchester United produced two spirited fightbacks to avoid defeat and potentially prolong Carrick’s reign as manager.

Goals from Brazilian winger Alysson and Senegal striker Nicolas Jackson put Villa 2-0 up inside five minutes but the hosts were level by half-time thanks to Bruno Fernandes’ penalty and Youri Tielemans equaliser against his former club.

John McGinn restored Aston Villa’s lead just after half-time and the visitors appeared to have the game wrapped up when Leon Goretzka scored a fourth on 53 minutes.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But injury-time goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu saw Manchester United salvage a point and avoid a third successive league defeat.

The comeback rivalled the one United produced in the Champions League against Roma during the week but it remains to be seen whether it saves Carrick his job.

Despite avoiding defeat, the Red Devils slip to 18th in the Premier League after ten games, their lowest position at the stage of a campaign since 1986.

Carrick’s side have also gone eight league games without a win, matching a run they have endured just once before in the Premier League.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I’m disappointed that we haven’t won the game,’ Carrick said. ‘We looked the better team for long parts of it and we’re making it difficult for ourselves with the goals that we’re giving away.

‘We’re not just giving away one, it’s two in succession that put us in such a difficult position. We did it the other night, we did it again today and have come back into the game and had a lot of the game, could have won it at the end.

‘So I’m disappointed we haven’t won the game. It’s just moments that we need to tighten up on. Individual moments where we’re giving teams goals that we don’t normally get.

‘If we tighten up that, there’s a lot of good in that performance. I thought we should have won the game. But conceding the goals we are is not helping us at all.

"That's not going to happen" 🗣️Michael Carrick responds to the notion that he could resign as Manchester United head coach 🔴 pic.twitter.com/q1fBKSXL7l

‘We have got to tighten up, it’s pretty obvious to say that. It’s giving us too much to do in games. But I thought we did a lot and feel that we should have won the game.’

Asked whether he feels Manchester United are in a relegation battle, Carrick added: ‘We’re in November. I don’t like this situation or the results but we can definitely do something about it.’

Responding to Carrick’s post-match interview, former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said: ‘It’s obviously difficult for the manager. He’s under pressure, no doubt

‘He talks a lot but doesn’t say much. I don’t know if that’s a tactic. Like a politician. He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there’s things we need to work on.

‘But they better get moving on that. It’s the worst start in how many years, all these stats aren’t very good. If you keep giving up goals and chances, it’s just going to continue.

‘What are we expecting to change over the next few weeks and months? What are they working on? They need to do a lot better than that.’

While Manchester United slipped into the relegation zone, Aston Villa stay 10th after extending their unbeaten league run to seven games.

‘They had to bring the transfer budget forward and bring defenders in.’

Gary’s brother Phil, who also enjoyed incredible success at Manchester United as a player, added: ‘The back-four that finished the game – Mazraoui, Yoro, Heaven and Dorgu – that gets you relegated.

"Should be banging heads!" 😡Roy Keane discusses how Manchester United can improve their form pic.twitter.com/r7JZzj62LD

‘That back-four gets you the sack as a manager and that back-four cannot keep United, I don’t think, in the Premier League.

‘That back-four gets you relegated, it’s poor. It’s not good enough to play in the Premier League.’

Despite Manchester United’s grim position in the Premier League, Gary Neville doubts a change in the dugout would improve the situation in the long-term.

‘You can paper over the cracks and get a new manager bounce,’ he added. ‘When the new manager comes in, everybody’s happy for a couple of months and all of a sudden, six months later, it happens again.

‘You can keep changing the manager and thinking that’s going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years, that’s not the answer.

‘Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don’t know, the ownership don’t have a clue what to do.

‘It’s rinse and repeat. Amorim, Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick – some of them are world class managers who have had success, there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex players who know the club as well.

‘None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you’ve got poor performance department, poor recruitment department, you’ve not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club you will fail.

‘Every organisation in the world will fail if you’ve not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom – your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football.

‘There are real issues within that football club, you’ve got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions.’

#1896. Man United: Every Big Six club's worst Premier League finish after Red Devils plunge into relegation zone

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 08 Nov 2026 12:50

Manchester United have struggled for much of the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era, but they appear to have reached a new low in the 2026-27 Premier League campaign.

Although the Red Devils finished 15th in 2024-25 and were struggling again the following season before Ruben Amorim's dismissal, Michael Carrick inspired a second-half revival that saw them finish third, earning him the permanent manager's job.

However, the former England midfielder has endured a difficult start to his first full campaign in charge, with just one win from their opening nine top-flight games and none in their last seven, leaving the 20-time league champions in a precarious position.

Nottingham Forest's 3-1 victory over Manchester City on Saturday had a knock-on effect on the Premier League table, pushing United down to 18th and into the relegation zone ahead of their gameweek 10 clash with Aston Villa later on Sunday, marking their first time in the bottom three nine games into a season since 1986.

Things could get even worse if Crystal Palace avoid defeat at home to Liverpool and Sunderland beat Chelsea, as that combination would leave United bottom of the table before they even take to the pitch at Old Trafford.

With the situation looking increasingly unusual for a club of United's stature, attention turns to the other heavyweights who have found themselves in trouble, and Sports Mole looks at the worst Premier League finish of every traditional top-six side, ranked from worst to best.

City's failure to win the Premier League title in back-to-back seasons in 2024-25 and 2025-26 felt like an anomaly for a club that had claimed six crowns in seven years under Pep Guardiola, but the Citizens have not always enjoyed such lofty standards.

Before Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan's takeover in 2008, City spent much of their time in mid-table and twice finished 18th in the Premier League era, suffering relegation on both occasions.

The first came in 1995-96 under Alan Ball, whose side collected just two points from their opening 11 league games before finishing the campaign with 38 points, having won nine, drawn 11 and lost 18.

The outcome went down to the final day, when City came from 2-0 down against Liverpool at half time to draw 2-2, but they were still relegated on goal difference after Ball, believing a draw would be enough, had his players run down the clock.

The Cityzens’ second relegation came in 2000-01 under Joe Royle, following back-to-back promotions, with a 4-0 opening-day defeat to Charlton Athletic setting the tone for a difficult campaign and marquee signing George Weah leaving in October after just 11 appearances.

Relegation was confirmed with defeat at Ipswich Town, leading to Royle's dismissal, before Kevin Keegan took charge and guided City straight back up as Division One champions, although it remained their third relegation in six years, a period that had also seen them drop into the third tier in 1998.

Tottenham's worst Premier League finish has now come in successive seasons, with Spurs ending both 2024-25 and 2025-26 in 17th place.

In 2024-25, Ange Postecoglou's injury-hit side lost 22 of their 38 league games, becoming the first top-flight team to suffer that many defeats and still avoid relegation, finishing on 38 points.

Remarkably, the campaign still ended with the club lifting their first European trophy in 41 years, courtesy of a 1-0 victory over Manchester United in the Europa League final in Bilbao, although Postecoglou was sacked just 16 days later.

The following season brought even more turmoil, as Thomas Frank was dismissed in February 2026 after an eight-game winless run left Spurs 16th, before Igor Tudor lasted just 44 days prior to his own departure.

Roberto De Zerbi was then handed a long-term contract with relegation looming, and victories over Wolverhampton Wanderers and Aston Villa gave Spurs renewed hope heading into the final day.

A 1-0 home win over Everton took them to 41 points and kept them in 17th place, sending West Ham United down on 39 points despite their 3-0 victory over Leeds United.

United's lowest Premier League finish came just two seasons ago, when they ended the 2024-25 campaign in 15th place with 42 points and 44 goals scored, both representing club lows.

Erik ten Hag was sacked in October 2024 after just nine league games, only months after signing a contract extension, with Ruud van Nistelrooy taking temporary charge before Amorim inherited a side sitting 12th in the table.

Matters deteriorated further under the Portuguese coach, who admitted in January 2025 that his team might be the worst in the club's history, with United suffering 18 league defeats that season, their highest tally since being relegated in 1973-74.

The Red Devils also failed to win consecutive league games throughout the campaign for the first time in the club's history before ending the season with defeat to Spurs in the Europa League final, leaving them without European football the following term.

United bounced back to finish third under Carrick in 2025-26, but their return to the bottom three just nine games into the current campaign has made that 15th-placed finish look rather less like a low point.

Chelsea's worst Premier League finish came in 1993-94, when they ended the 42-game season in 14th place with 51 points from 13 wins, 12 draws and 17 defeats.

Glenn Hoddle's arrival as player-manager had raised hopes after previous bosses had struggled to take the club beyond mid-table, but the league campaign never really gathered momentum.

The season included an 11-game winless run, while a 4-1 defeat at Leeds United proved their heaviest loss of the campaign.

There was some consolation in the cups, with Gavin Peacock scoring twice in the semi-final victory over Luton Town to send Chelsea into their first FA Cup final in 24 years.

Man United ran out 4-0 winners in the final, with Eric Cantona scoring twice, but their status as league champions meant they were heading for the Champions League, leaving Chelsea to take the Cup Winners' Cup place as runners-up.

The campaign proved to be the beginning of a rebuild that would eventually bring Ruud Gullit to Stamford Bridge.

Arsenal entered the 1994-95 campaign as a club accustomed to winning trophies, having claimed the league title in 1991, both domestic cups in 1993 and the Cup Winners' Cup in 1994, yet they finished 12th, their lowest league placing since 1976.

The season began poorly, with the Gunners scoring in just one of their opening five league games, and they never managed to escape mid-table, eventually finishing on 51 points in a 42-game campaign, just six clear of the relegation zone.

George Graham was sacked on February 21, 1995, after it emerged that he had accepted a £425,000 payment from agent Rune Hauge, and he was subsequently banned from football for a year by the FA.

Assistant Stewart Houston stepped in and won his first two games, but his arrival coincided with a run of six defeats in seven matches that left Arsenal in real danger of relegation.

The threat was greater than usual because four clubs were going down that season as the Premier League prepared to reduce from 22 teams to 20.

Arsenal at least had Ian Wright's 18 league goals and a run to the Cup Winners' Cup final to take some encouragement from, but Nayim's remarkable lob from more than 40 yards over David Seaman in the closing seconds of extra time handed Real Zaragoza the trophy.

Liverpool are the only traditional top-six side never to have finished below eighth in the Premier League era, although they have ended the campaign in that position on three occasions.

The first came in 1993-94, when Graeme Souness resigned in January following a home FA Cup defeat to Bristol City, leaving bootroom stalwart Roy Evans to take charge.

That campaign marked Robbie Fowler's breakthrough season and the final year of the Kop as a standing terrace, but it also saw Liverpool suffer 16 league defeats, their highest tally in a Premier League season.

In 2011-12, Kenny Dalglish's side collected 52 points, their lowest total since 1954, in a campaign overshadowed by Luis Suarez's eight-match ban for racially abusing Patrice Evra and lengthy injury absences for Lucas Leiva and Steven Gerrard.

The Merseyside Reds did lift the League Cup, beating Cardiff City on penalties to end a six-year trophy drought, but won only four of their next 11 league games and lost the FA Cup final to Chelsea, a run of results that ultimately cost Dalglish his job.

The third eighth-placed finish came in 2015-16, when Brendan Rodgers was sacked in October with Liverpool sitting 10th, before Jurgen Klopp took over four days later and guided the Reds to two finals, only to lose both against Man City on penalties and Sevilla.

#1895. Michael Carrick speaks out on Diogo Dalot future after Manchester United fans make feelings clear

Manchester United fans made their frustrations with Diogo Dalot very clear at Old Trafford on Sunday, but Michael Carrick has defended the under-fire full-back.

The bizarre match finished 4-4 with Aston Villa, as the visitors twice relinquished a two-goal lead to their struggling hosts.

Alysson and Nicolas Jackson had put the Villains 2-0 up within five minutes, only for Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans to put the Red Devils level by half-time.

Villa were two goals in front by 53 minutes as John McGinn and Leon Goretzka started the second half brilliantly and Old Trafford was stunned again.

However, Carrick’s men pulled off a remarkable escape in stoppage time as substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dourgu both scored after the 90-minute mark to rescue a point.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Dorgu replaced Dalot on 66 minutes after a nightmare performance from the Portugal international, which included conceding a penalty for felling Alysson, leading to McGinn’s goal from the spot.

When his number came up there were loud cheers from supporters at Old Trafford, which turned to boos as he left the field.

The 27-year-old has played in all 10 of Manchester United’s Premier League fixtures this season but when Carrick was asked if it was time for him to come out of the team, he pushed back and defended the full-back.

‘We’ve got to be careful with that, I think,’ said the Red Devils boss.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I understand the frustration and the disappointment of the supporters. I get it, we’re all frustrated, we’re all disappointed. The players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

‘Diogo gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions, he’s played really well at times.

‘He gives the penalty away today, he knows that. Maybe he can do a little bit better, alright, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake.

‘He cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything. I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking a team and who plays the next game that’s a whole different decision and that’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’

Dalot signed for Manchester United in 2018 and has become something of a symbol of the mediocrity that fans have watched since then.

Gary Neville, who knows plenty about playing full-back for Manchester United, defended Dalot from criticism earlier this year, saying in January on his Sky Sports podcast: ‘He gets a really harsh view at times [from] quite a few United fans. I do think there’s a half-decent full-back in there, and I watch full-backs so closely.

‘I think he’s actually good in the air. I think he’s got good athleticism about him. I think he’s decent on the ball. I don’t think he’s a world-class full-back, but neither was I.’

He added: ‘I think he’s got something about him. I think he’s got 7/10 in him every single week, Dalot, but because we’ve seen him at left wing-back, we’ve seen him at right wing-back, we’ve seen him exposed so many times.

‘I think if he just played right full-back and played there all the time, I wouldn’t be getting rid of him in a hurry.

‘Now, other people might disagree with me, but I think I know the position of full-back, and I think he could do a decent job for Manchester United.’

Neville was not complimentary about the United defence on Sunday, though, saying on NBC Sports: ‘The reason that Manchester United have conceded four goals is they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window.

‘Everybody knew they had to invest in the defence. They needed defenders. They’re making mistake after mistake after mistake.’

The draw with Villa means Manchester United have won just one of their opening 10 games of the Premier League season and sit 18th in the table.

#1894. Man United co-owner Avram Glazer 'says they don't NEED success on the pitch to make money' - just like the New York Yankees and Dallas Cowboys

Published: 06:18 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 06:48 EST, 5 November 2026

Manchester United co-owner Avram Glazer has claimed the club’s value is not dependent on success on the pitch.

The figurehead of the hugely unpopular Glazer family addressed an audience at Deutsche Bank’s inaugural Sports Investment Conference in London.

The topic of United’s underperformance on the pitch and whether there is a clear link between on-pitch performance and commercial success came up from an audience member and Glazer was robust in response.

According to the Athletic, the United co-chairman is said to have likened the club to major sporting franchises and brands such as the Dallas Cowboys and the New York Yankees, two teams that haven’t won the Super Bowl or the World Series for years. The Cowboys were last victorious in 1996, and the Yankees in 2009.

United, who haven’t won a Premier League title since 2013 when Sir Alex Ferguson departed, have a rich history as one of the biggest teams in the world but have fallen on hard times in recent years on the pitch, leading to major protests against the Glazer ownership.

United are 17th in the Premier League heading into Sunday’s home game against Aston Villa, hovering precariously above the relegation zone. Any relegation, however unlikely, would be financially devastating.

According to the Glazers, Manchester United's value is not dependent on success on the pitch

It's no wonder Red Devils fans have lost faith in the Glazer family's ownership of their club

But Glazer, who was speaking at the event in September but whose remarks have only just come to light, remains bullish that United are shielded from much fluctuation in their commercial revenue due to the scale of the club's brand around the world.

United’s commercial revenue has continued to rise, even in the lean post-Ferguson years.

In 2012-13, commercial revenue stood at £152m, and by 2017-18 it was £276m. The 2025-26 figure reported was £317m.

While the United brand remains incredibly strong due to its support around the world and the club’s rich history, performance has knocked them down in terms of financial superiority.

Forbes, a go-to list used by the Glazers, ranked United as the third most valuable club in May of this year, behind Real Madrid and Barcelona. A year prior, only Real Madrid were ahead of them.

For context, United were top of the pile as recently as 2018 and owned that spot for a five-year stretch between 2007 and 2012.

Debt is at the centre of United supporters’ frustration with the Glazers, who leveraged money from banks to take over the club in 2005, with the total debt coming in at £689million as recently as June. That’s a steep increase on the previous year of £52m and it shows no sign of going away.

Ineos have been brought in as a minority owner and while Sir Jim Ratcliffe and his team dictate football decisions, and have done since February 2024, Avram and Joel Glazer remain at the centre of budgets and other key decisions.

Bruno Fernandes celebrates as United stop the rot with a superb comeback win against Roma

Comments made by Glazer in September at this convention for financiers only reinforce what many supporters believe and that’s that the Glazer family are not interested in sporting success and instead only focus on the balance sheet.

Ahead of Tuesday night’s win over Roma in the Champions League, 2,000 green and gold balloons – the colours synonymous with the fans’ protests against the Glazer ownership – filled the Stretford End and tennis balls were later thrown towards the pitch.

In recent weeks, with results and performances on the slide after a summer transfer window that left Michael Carrick short compared to rivals, fans have started to escalate chants against the Glazers, director of football Jason Wilcox and Ineos, calling for them to ‘sell United and f*** off home’.

A rousing rendition of ‘stand up if you hate Glazers’ also whipped Old Trafford into a frenzy before United’s players pulled an unlikely win out of the hat on the pitch to keep hopes of progressing in the Champions League alive.

The other side of this is that Glazer may well have been trying to be bullish in the face of finance folk and investors given the rather bleak debt picture.

That won’t be how it’s viewed in Manchester, though, and it does little to give fans hope that the majority owner and minority owner are both seemingly taking this club in the wrong direction.

#1892. Michael Carrick told Man Utd star was ‘playing for himself’ in Aston Villa draw

Troy Deeney took aim at Amad Diallo following Manchester United’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, claiming the winger ‘flattered to deceive’ and appeared to be ‘playing for himself’.

United twice fought back from two goals down to come away from Old Trafford with a point in Sunday’s thriller at Old Trafford, but the result saw Michael Carrick’s men enter the international break in the relegation zone.

The hosts were punished for their sluggishness early on as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson made it 2-0 inside only four minutes, only for Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans to find the net and draw level.

The Red Devils were once again punished for a slow start, though, as John McGinn converted a 48th-minute penalty before Leon Goretzka capitalised on some calamitous defending from Leny Yoro to restore the visitors’ two-goal cushion.

Staring down the barrel of a fifth Premier League defeat, Carrick rang the changes in search of a route back into the contest in the second half – and it was two of United’s substitutes, Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, who struck to salvage a draw at the death.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But with his side hovering just one point above rock-bottom Crystal Palace, Carrick will know the scrutiny and speculation surrounding his future is likely to rumble on ahead of the club’s crunch match away to bitter rivals Liverpool in a fortnight’s time.

‘I spoke about this on our last episode on Thursday, I feel like we’re doing the same things with Manchester United,’ ex-Watford and Birmingham striker Deeney said of United’s latest performance on talkSPORT’s Premier League All Access Podcast.

There had been calls for Carrick to field Shea Lacey in place of Amad following the youngster’s outstanding cameo display in United’s midweek Champions League victory over Roma.

However, the United head coach stuck to his guns and kept faith with Amad, who would go on to have a tough afternoon at the Theatre of Dreams.

‘Amad comes in and flatters to deceive,’ Deeney said of the Ivorian’s display.

‘A lot of running into nothing, he was… today it felt like a lot of them were playing for themselves and going, “Look, I’m not the problem!”

‘Amad had about nine shots in the first half that were never going to be on target.’

On United’s problems in the centre of the park, Deeney continued: ‘I saw a midfield that was empty and vacated today.

‘Villa went through that midfield at will, many times in that first 75 minutes.’

Unai Emery made five substitutions before United’s late fightback, with goalscorers McGinn, Alysson, Goretzka and Jackson all removed, as well as the lively Johan Manzambi.

Asked whether the Villa manager had made a mistake with his changes, Deeney replied: ‘Absolutely.

‘I also thought it was one of the few times where he’d probably be very disappointed and would want to go back when you look at taking off Johan Manzambi, who I thought was excellent.

‘His ability to not only roll the player and keep the ball, but buy fouls and take them ten, 15, 20 yards up the pitch was excellent.

‘I think the game got too easy for Villa at 4-2 and I thought Emery started to think a little bit too far ahead, “Okay, I can rest these players”, obviously going away to international break.

‘Nicolas Jackson at times looked like Kylian Mbappe against that Manchester United team. He was dropping team, running in behind, he was 15 yards away from everyone.

‘But I just think he made too many mistakes and you can’t account for a goalkeeper having a shocker as well.’

Diogo Dalot appeared to be targeted with sarcastic cheers from the Old Trafford crowd when he was replaced for Dorgu midway through the second half.

Facing the media shortly after the final whistle, Carrick jumped to Dalot’s defence and encouraged supporters to get behind the players, especially when they are playing out of position.

‘Diogo, he gives absolutely everything,’ Carrick said.

‘He’s played in different positions, he’s played left-back, he’s played really well at times. He gives a penalty away today, that’s, you know, he knows that.

‘Maybe he can do a little bit better, all right, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake, but he cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything.’

On Dalot, the United boss went on: ‘I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking a team and who plays the next game, that’s a whole different decision, but it’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’

#1891. Aston Villa chief points finger at Manchester United star after controversial incident

Aston Villa’s Director of Football Operations has hit out at the controversial decision to let Manchester United’s equaliser on Sunday stand.

A thrilling contest at Old Trafford finished 4-4 as the home side scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an unlikely point.

Villa went 2-0 ahead within five minutes thanks to goals from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson, before Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans leveled things up before the break.

The Red Devils started the second half as badly as they did the first as John McGinn scored from the penalty spot before Leon Goretzka made it 4-2 on 53 minutes.

As the clock ticked past 90 minutes it looked bleak for Michael Carrick, but substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scored in injury time to give the home fans something to cheer.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Dorgu’s headed goal was not without controversy as Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki claimed he was impeded by his opposite number Senne Lammens who was up for the corner.

Manchester United legend Roy Keane did not think it was a foul by the Belgian, saying on Sky Sports: ‘I don’t think Suzuki gives himself the best chance of getting it, he’s underneath it, just take a step back and attack it. There are bodies in the way, but there’s lots going on, football is a contact sport. I have no problem with it.

"Football is a contact sport!" 🗣️Did Senne Lammens foul Zion Suzuki for Man United's equaliser? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/KCb1lHqPHP

‘A goalkeeper in this situation, he should take command of it. If he’s talking about getting blocked and pushed, why doesn’t he do that to the opposition players?

‘He’s got to come and be aggressive. When the ball comes in he’s on his heels. He’s got to be more aggressive and take command of that six-yard box.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The incident will split opinion as Lammens seemed to look at Suzuki, turn his back to him and then purposefully nudge him with no attempt to play the ball.

That was certainly the stance of Damian Vidagany, who says referees had vowed to be harsher on such incidents.

Posting on X, Villa’s Director of Football Operations wrote: ‘To put in context this convenient narrative of “contact sport” we’ve been told by referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six hard box was not going to be allowed anymore.

‘Lammens not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion.

‘Having said that we played good match and we must do better than last 6 minutes. We will do and we will improve. But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact.’

Villa boss Unai Emery said his 24-year-old goalkeeper, who arrived from Parma over the summer, is still getting used to Premier League officiating, which is different to elsewhere.

‘When we are conceding the last goal in this corner, it is adaptation,’ he told Sky Sports. ‘Adaptation to the Premier League for Zion to settle here well. He must try to, because it is not the same timing. Here is not foul. They are pushing, they are disturbing the keeper.

‘Of course, in another countries, another leagues, they are not permitting it. Here, yes. We have to continue analysing, having experiences, and trying to avoid situation like we conceded.’

#1890. Sunderland suffer Granit Xhaka injury blow against Chelsea as Regis Le Bris forced into early change

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 14:17, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 14:37

Sunderland were dealt a major injury concern just a few minutes into their Premier League clash with Chelsea, as Granit Xhaka was forced off with a suspected calf problem.

The former Arsenal man unsurprisingly started the Stadium of Light encounter against the Blues, who were interested in signing him during the summer transfer window.

Xhaka ultimately snubbed interest from the West London giants to remain with Sunderland, but he did not get the chance to show his former admirers what they are missing out on.

With just a couple of minutes gone on Sunday afternoon, the Switzerland international dropped to the turf and eventually had to hobble off after receiving treatment.

Xhaka - who was replaced by Jules Ahoka - appeared to have sustained a calf problem, although he was able to take his place on the bench shortly after being withdrawn.

Regis Le Bris will be quizzed for an update on Xhaka's injury at full time, but Sunderland will need to send the midfielder for tests to determine the severity of his problem.

However, if Xhaka has suffered a calf injury as expected, the 34-year-old's recuperation period could range from a couple of weeks to a few months depending on the grade of his concern.

A Grade 1 issue - or mild strain - usually takes one to two weeks to heal, meaning that Xhaka could return in time for Sunderland's clash with Aston Villa on November 21 following the international break.

A Grade 2 injury could rule Xhaka out for up to six weeks, though, putting him at risk of missing games against Jagiellonia Bialystok, Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool, Newcastle United, AC Milan, Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace between now and Christmas.

Meanwhile, a Grade 3 injury - a complete tear - would likely sideline Xhaka for three months, forcing him to sit out clashes with Manchester United, Chelsea and Liverpool either side of the New Year.

Xhaka was making his 14th appearance of the season for Sunderland in all competitions before being withdrawn, and he played the full 90 minutes in each of the Black Cats' first nine Premier League matches of the campaign.

Le Bris is already without fellow midfielder Habib Diarra due to a thigh injury, and the 22-year-old is not anticipated to return before the middle of December.

With Diarra on the sidelines, Ahoka is the most natural alternative to Xhaka alongside Noah Sadiki, although Le Bris could also consider a couple of emergency options amid the hectic schedule.

Enzo Le Fee could start in a deeper position, as could Chris Rigg, although Sunderland are already lighter in attack with Romaine Mundle (knee) out until 2027.

Alternatively, Le Bris could bring 31-year-old midfielder Alan Browne back into the fold; the Irishman spent last season on loan at Middlesbrough and has been restricted to just two EFL Cup appearances for Sunderland so far this season.

#1887. Manchester United flops hit with ‘non-league’ jibe from Arsenal legend

Manchester United’s defending against Aston Villa ‘wouldn’t be seen in non-league’ football, says Martin Keown, who asks if the club is ‘sleepwalking into relegation.’

The Red Devils escaped with a point after an incredible 4-4 draw at Old Trafford on Sunday after twice falling behind by two goals.

Alysson and Nicolas Jackson both scored in the opening five minutes, before Manchester United fought back to level before half-time through Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans.

The second half started as badly as the first for the home team, with John McGinn and Leon Goretzka putting the Villains 4-2 up on 53 minutes.

The clock ticked past 90 minutes and that scoreline remained, before substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scored in injury time to compete a chaotic contest.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Michael Carrick’s team has won just one of the first 10 Premier League games this season, sitting 18th in the table with eight points accrued.

Keown saw the Manchester United defence as fearful and not at a level anywhere near the Premier League, left with the feeling that relegation is a genuine concern.

‘Are they sleepwalking into relegation? You’re 10 games in, one win. All competitions, 40 goals conceded,’ Keown said on talkSPORT.

‘Defending, you wouldn’t see that in the non-league that I saw yesterday, honestly. The goalkeeper making mistakes, he’s joining in now. I smell fear across that back four.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Keown accepts that Manchester United showed some fight to respond at the death and also did so in their win over Roma earlier in the week, but thinks something is ‘very wrong’ with a team that continues to fall behind in matches.

‘Okay, I saw character and personality and saw it in midweek,’ said the former England defender. ‘But when you win a game like that against Roma, you have to put that in a bottle and channel all that energy from the first whistle against Villa and they were two goals down in each half within minutes.

‘Something is very wrong. The players are not motivated. You can’t keep coming back from the brink in the way that they did. Okay you’ll say that’s a bit of personality, but something is the wrong with the team and the way it defends.’

Carrick was not too down on his team’s performance overall, but insisted that it is just ‘moments’ that are costing Manchester United.

‘There was a lot happened in the game,’ he said. ‘It’s just the moments that are making it [difficult]. We’re kind of beating ourselves a little bit, with the moments that we’re giving away and goals that we’re giving away in tight clusters, that are making it a lot more difficult.

‘It’s hard enough anyway, but making it a lot more difficult than it should be. Football’s about moments. Football’s about what happens in both boxes in the end.

‘I think you take the moments that are totally avoidable, goals that we’re giving away, I actually thought we’ve played pretty well and were the better team for the most part, and I’m disappointed that we still haven’t won the game, to be truthful.

‘I thought we had most of the pressure. I thought we defended well, pressed well. We’re just giving them the moments that shape the game in some ways and then finished strongly and took something out of the game but still disappointing that we haven’t actually won it.’

He added: ‘It’s moments that are really causing us the problem. So if we can deal with that, a little bit of concentration, a little bit of confidence, a little bit of belief, a little bit of mentality, all that comes into making the right decisions

‘I’d say the last three games or so, there’s good things that give us a lot of encouragement that we can definitely win a lot of football matches with, and I feel like we should’ve won today even though we’ve still give too much away.’

#1884. Man United, Arsenal handed huge early suspension boosts after Igor Thiago VAR decision

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 14:46, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 15:02

Manchester United and Arsenal have been handed huge early boosts for their Premier League clashes with Brentford, which Igor Thiago will miss through suspension.

The Brazil international started up top for the Bees in their trip to Brighton & Hove Albion, but things quickly unravelled for Keith Andrews's side at the Amex Stadium.

Brentford fell 1-0 down within 15 minutes to a Diego Gomez goal, before Thiago and Chema Andres were involved in a set-to, which saw Thiago shove the Brighton man in the face.

The striker was initially booked for his role in the incident, but upon reviewing the incident on the pitchside monitor, referee Michael Oliver issued a straight red card to Thiago.

"After review, Brentford No.9 pushes his opponent in the face with force. Yellow card is cancelled and the final decision is red card," Oliver announced to the crowd, as Thiago prepares to serve a three-game suspension.

Brentford are a goal down and now a man down ? Igor Thiago is sent off after a VAR review. Referee Michael Oliver says he pushed Brighton's Chema Andres "in the face with force." https://t.co/YMZrYFUGyx

As the Brentford man was dismissed for violent conduct, he will be forced to sit out the Bees' next three matches against Everton, Man United and Arsenal after the international break.

Thiago begins his ban against Everton on November 23, before Andrews's men travel to Man United on November 28, and he completes his suspension against champions Arsenal on December 2.

The 25-year-old's punishment could be revoked if Brentford are successful with an appeal, but it is extremely unlikely that the Bees would win their case if they decided to contest the decision.

Andrews will therefore have to cope without his chief centre-forward for crunch clashes with Arsenal and Man Utd, although Thiago has so far struggled to replicate his 22-goal form from 2025-26.

The South American has scored just two goals and set up two more in 10 Premier League games this season, although each one of those contributions came in his last five full appearances.

Thiago's absence is especially untimely for Brentford, as Andrews is also working without another striker - 19-year-old Kaye Furo - due to a serious foot injury.

Furo has made "really good progress" in his recuperation, though, and there is a chance that the 2007-born striker could be ready for competitive action following the international break.

However, Thiago's ban could instead open the door for 34-year-old veteran Callum Wilson to make his first Premier League starts of the season, as the Englishman has made just six substitute appearances in the 2026-27 English top flight so far.

Dango Ouattara and Kevin Schade could also be deployed as auxiliary centre-forwards, but Thiago's absence nevertheless represents a major blow for Brentford, and a major boost for Arsenal and Man Utd.

#1883. Why Tottenham's 'rock' Jan Paul van Hecke is being compared to Bobby Moore and Stuart Pearce: 'Releasing the beast', a 'Zeeland Army' watching his every move and how high-risk passing is paying off

Published: 07:00 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 07:14 EST, 5 November 2026

With his roots in a humble fishing community, World Cup pedigree in the family and glowing comparisons to a couple of England legends, it is perhaps no surprise to find Jan Paul van Hecke emerging as Tottenham's anchorman after a turbulent start to the season.

Van Hecke's strength of character shone through when things went badly awry and Spurs sank to the bottom of the Premier League, winless in the first five games, then rose from the depths with 10 points from the next four.

His ability and influence would never have been in doubt as far as Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi was concerned, having worked with Van Hecke for two years at Brighton. The 26-year-old Dutch centre-half leaves a positive impression wherever he plays.

'JP is a real force,' says Peter Maas, technical director of NAC Breda, where Van Hecke began his professional career. 'He is a rock. He will never back off. He will never let his team down. Never, never. He is truly one of a kind. A good lad with a good heart.

'I've always compared his presence and commitment to Stuart Pearce, "Psycho" back in the '80s and '90s. He was crazy, eh? Every now and then, JP will release the beast and let everything out.

'But he can play football, too. He can defend in an old-school way, but he can also build play in the modern way and is certainly more composed now.'

Jan Paul van Hecke has been Tottenham's anchorman this season, as they recovered from a woeful start to take 10 points from their last four league games

He tops Spurs' charts for clearances and duels won - as well as having completed more forward passes and more line-breaking passes than any other outfielder in the Premier League

Van Hecke's uncle Jan Poortvliet (centre, facing camera) was a defender in the Netherlands team which lost to Argentina in the 1978 World Cup final

Van Hecke's uncle Jan Poortvliet was a defender in the Netherlands team which made it to the World Cup final in 1978, and 30 years later had a brief spell as Southampton manager in the Championship. Jan Paul needs one more cap to match Poortvliet's tally of 19 for his country.

Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray, a fearless centre-half as a player, compared Van Hecke to another blond England legend after luring him to Ewood Park on loan from Brighton in 2021. The Seagulls had signed Van Hecke for £1.8million the year before and sold him to Spurs this summer for £54m.

'I've got to be careful I don't overbuild him as he's not our player,' said Mowbray at the time. 'But he looks like Bobby Moore out there sometimes. It's amazing to watch how composed, how calm he can be, yet he has the fire of a warrior in his belly.'

Van Hecke's vision and passing range combined with his natural aggression and appetite for sporting conflict appeals to the modern coach.

He meets the physical demands of the Premier League with relish, hailing from Arnemuiden, an isolated town of 5,000 in the province of Zeeland with a deep-rooted fishing history and a reputation for resilience through times of hardship.

It is now home to an army of devoted Van Hecke fans who cross the North Sea to watch him play at every opportunity. One hundred made the journey to see him score against Crystal Palace last Saturday.

Another element of Van Hecke's early impact in N17 has been his readiness to accept the ball, often in difficult areas, and search for forward passes through the lines.

It has led to mistakes which irritated some Spurs fans during their terrible start to the campaign, but De Zerbi demands this high-risk style and Van Hecke to his credit resisted the temptation to play with greater caution even though it would have spared him some of the criticism.

Van Hecke made such an impression on Tony Mowbray on loan at Blackburn in 2021-22 that he compared him to Bobby Moore

His impact is clear from his data. Van Hecke has played every minute of the Premier League campaign, starting the game at Manchester United last month despite returning from international duty with stitches in a wound on the top of his foot.

He has completed more forward passes (258) and more line-breaking passes (150) than any outfielder in the Premier League. Only Arsenal duo Martin Odegaard (197) and Declan Rice (177) have made more successful passes into the final third than his 174, only Manchester City's Ruben Dias (819) has played more passes than his 809, and Van Hecke leads the Spurs ranks for clearances and duels won. For good measure, he is also the club's top scorer – albeit with only two goals.

His desire to shoulder responsibility even in difficult times is exactly the type of leadership by example Spurs have lacked in recent years.

'He excelled in one-on-one defending but above all in his mentality,' Maas tells Daily Mail Sport as he reflects on Van Hecke's early development after joining NAC from amateur team VV Goes at the age of 18.

'What struck me was that when faced with setbacks, or a kick or a blow to the head on the pitch, he always got back up with even greater determination. It was as if the adrenaline helped him become unbeatable.

'That's where he channelled his energy. First at NAC in the second tier, then at Heerenveen in the Eredivisie. At Brighton, too. Step by step, he gets 10 per cent better every time because he adapts easily to his surroundings.'

There were times when the teenage Van Hecke might display frustration to be on the fringes of the team at NAC. Competition for places at the back included Colin Rosler, a graduate of the Manchester City academy where his father Uwe was a hero and who now plays in Denmark for AGF.

'Until the winter of 2019, JP was mainly a substitute and clearly struggling with that,' recalls Maas, who left the head scout's role at NAC for the same post at Heerenveen in 2021 before returning as NAC technical director two years later.

Van Hecke is Spurs' top scorer in the Premier League this season - albeit with only two goals

'It was impossible to predict he would make the upper echelons of the Premier League and the Dutch national team,' says Maas. 'But you could certainly see he had great potential'

'He felt it was unfair that he wasn't playing and went through a rough patch and was showing it. He actually lost the will to play, and I held a mirror to him once during a chat in the players' lounge and told him he had to prove himself.'

Helped by a change of head coach, Van Hecke broke into the first team and became integral to second-tier NAC's run to the semi-finals of the Dutch Cup, beating PSV Eindhoven and AZ Alkmaar before losing to Feyenoord.

His success came to personify the fighting spirit of NAC and he became the poster boy for their prolific youth development programme, with Bart Verbruggen, Van Hecke's team-mate at Brighton, also a graduate.

'It was impossible to predict he would make the upper echelons of the Premier League and the Dutch national team,' says Maas. 'But you could certainly see he had great potential and he will continue to improve because his immense drive will take him further.'

#1877. Ipswich vs. Bournemouth: Evanilson makes history after shocking goalkeeper error

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 15:12, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 15:26

Evanilson etched his name into the Bournemouth history books by opening the scoring in Sunday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town.

The Brazil international came into the Portman Road battle in hot goalscoring form, having netted in four top-flight games in succession.

However, Evanilson was gifted one of the easiest goals he will ever score in English football against Ipswich, thanks to a shocking mistake from Tractor Boys goalkeeper Christian Walton.

Under pressure from Evanilson, Walton attempted to drag the ball away from the Bournemouth striker rather than clearing his lines, but he was robbed of possession by the South American.

Evanilson evaded Walton's desperate sprawling grasp and slotted the ball into an empty net, thus becoming the first Bournemouth player in history to score in five straight Premier League games.

It's Evanilson again for Bournemouth! ? A nightmare for Christian Walton and Evanilson makes no mistake https://t.co/QYGU9Xaniv

The 27-year-old's scoring sequence began on October 10, when he netted the Cherries' consolation goal in their 5-1 hammering at the hands of Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

Evanilson then found the net in each of his three remaining Premier League games in October, helping to propel Bournemouth to victory against Sunderland, Manchester United and Leeds United.

The Brazilian failed to score in any of his first five league appearances of the campaign, but he has now moved onto nine direct involvements from his first 10 games, having also chalked up four assists.

Evanilson has also registered three goal contributions from four Europa League games - two of his own and one assist - while managing 12 in total across 14 outings in all tournaments.

Following the South American's early opener, Bournemouth doubled their lead on the stroke of half time through a Leif Davis own goal, putting Marco Rose's men on the verge of a fourth successive Premier League victory.

By making the net bulge at Portman Road, Evanilson moved above Junior Stanislas into outright seventh place in Bournemouth's all-time Premier League scoring charts.

The Brazilian is now just one behind teammate Justin Kluivert and two adrift of Marcus Tavernier, who is the highest active scorer in the Cherries' squad with 23 to his name.

Dominic Solanke's 28 and Antoine Semenyo's 30 are also within reach for Evanilson this season, but the Brazilian may need to wait a while longer to surpass Callum Wilson's 41 or Josh King's unparalleled 48.

Eli Junior Kroupi is further down the list in 10th place, but the much-coveted Frenchman boasts the best goals-per-game ratio of any Bournemouth Premier League player with 0.37.

#1876. Michael Carrick told four players that will 'RELEGATE' Manchester United and cost him his job

Gary and Phil Neville both believe that Manchester United’s current defence will drag the club into a relegation battle.

Michael Carrick’s struggling side twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa on Sunday, rallying back on both occasions to secure a chaotic last-gasp 4-4 draw at Old Trafford.

Manchester United have now conceded 19 goals in just 10 Premier League games this season, leaving the Red Devils sitting in the relegation zone heading into the final international break of 2026.

Gary Neville was a guest pundit on NBC Sports for the draw with Villa, with the ex-Man Utd captain criticising the club’s recruitment over the summer.

After spending around £200million on overhauling their attack in the summer of 2025, United focused on rebuilding their midfield ahead of the 2026/27 season.

But Neville believes that the club should have spent more in order to also fix their leaky defence.

He said: “The reason Manchester United have conceded four goals is because they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window.

“Every one knew they had to do that, they needed defenders. The current ones are making mistake after mistake after mistake.

“The defenders that finished that game will get you relegated. Watch the defensive errors. We all screamed in the transfer window that they have to bring some defenders in.

“They had to bring the transfer budget forward and bring defenders in.”

United have not signed a senior defender since bringing attack-minded wing-back Patrick Dorgu to the club in January 2025.

#1875. Paul Scholes blasts Man Utd players for ’embarrassing’ moment after Aston Villa draw

Paul Scholes has urged Manchester United’s struggling players to ditch ’embarrassing’ laps of honour after games.

The Red Devils are sitting 18th in the Premier League going into the November international break after winning just one of their ten games so far this season.

The last time United were in such a low position at this stage of the season was in 1986, while their record of eight league games without a win has only happened once before in the club’s history.

Michael Carrick and the Manchester United squad walked around the pitch applauding the fans following a humbling 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the end of last month.

Carrick was serenaded by the United fans despite the club’s dismal position but the supportive chants soon turned to boos directed at the players once the ex-England midfielder made his way down the tunnel.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The squad performed a similar lap of appreciation after Sunday’s thrilling 4-4 draw with Aston Villa but Manchester United legend Scholes was less than impressed by the gesture.

‘I tell you one thing they need to do, stop doing these laps of honour after every game,’ Scholes said on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast.

‘What the f**k. It’s so bad. Jesus, it’s embarrassing. Every game’s like the last game of the season. Just get off!’

Fellow former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt added: ‘That’s pissing me off as well. A lap of honour after a draw…’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

United twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa but produced a spirited comeback to avoid a fifth defeat in ten Premier League games.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Gary Neville praised the ‘persistence’ of Carrick’s side but was also critical of the post-match scenes, claiming the players are ‘almost causing themselves emotional damage’.

‘You have got to admire their persistence, they kept going,’ Neville told NBC Sports. ‘The defensive errors were shocking and we’ll discuss that shortly.

‘But this lap around the pitch… I played for Manchester United 602 times and I always appreciated the fans at the end of the game.

‘But this pattern of them walking around the pitch after defeats by Bournemouth and a 4-4 at home against Aston Villa, it’s almost painful to watch. They’re almost causing themselves emotional damage.

‘This just can’t go on, can it? It’s absolutely desperate. Michael will be proud of them and the fans are singing his name because they love him but this is a really sorry situation.’

The hierarchy at Old Trafford are currently reviewing Carrick’s position and weighing up whether to make a change during the international break.

Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte have all been linked with the job, although Manchester United could yet show more faith in Carrick.

The Red Devils, sitting just one point above bottom place in the Premier League, return to action with a daunting trip to Anfield to face arch-rivals Liverpool.

#1873. Agony of tragic footballer's girlfriend, stuck alone, while he died in hospital: How family could not reach Jesus de Miguel's partner - after his father burst into tears at a bar watching the horror collision on TV

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER and GERARD COUZENS

Published: 20:03 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 08:03 EST, 5 November 2026

A friend of the Spanish footballer who died after a horror tackle this week has spoken of the heartbreak of the late sportsman's girlfriend, who had been watching the game with their one-year-old daughter.

Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, 30, died on Tuesday morning hours after receiving a flying knee to the chest from Andorra FC goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off before the match in Spain's second division was abandoned.

Yesterday, a post-mortem found De Miguel died from 'accidental chest trauma'. It is described in the preliminary report as a 'cause consistent with the player's death.' His funeral is due to be held today.

De Miguel's close friend Fernando Roman offered a tribute on social media and in an interview with Vamos a Ver.

Roman, who plays for Spanish side Talavera, explained that he had not been watching the match on Monday, but was alerted to it by his girlfriend after De Miguel had been injured by the tackle.

Roman had then been in contact with De Miguel's girlfriend Maria, who had been at the stadium with their one-year-old daughter Carla. Roman revealed she had been alone at the hospital and has been hit 'very hard' by the tragedy.

She was eventually joined by the De Miguel's parents, who travelled to Tenerife after being informed their son was in intensive care.

Close friend Fernando Roman (left) has revealed Jesus De Miguel's girlfriend Maria had been alone in hospital prior to de Miguel's death on Tuesday. Source: X/@ferroman9

A neighbour has said De Miguel's father (pictured right, with his mother, girlfriend and sister R-L) burst into tears after seeing the impact of the collision on television. (Source: Instagram/martitamig)

De Miguel died on Tuesday morning following a horrifying clash with Andorra FC goalkeeper Jesus Owono in a Spanish second division match

A neighbour of De Miguel's parents in Navahermosa told Y ahora Sonsoles that his father 'started crying' as soon as he saw the impact of the collision on television at his bar and immediately gathered his family to travel to Tenerife.

Roman told Vamos a Ver: 'Yesterday, my girlfriend and I were talking all afternoon and all night with María, his girlfriend, who was alone in the hospital.

'I've spoken with his girlfriend, and you can imagine how she is. Now we have to be with the family.

'We have to send our love to his family, to María, to his daughter Carla, who is a year and a few months old.

'It was unbelievable because we were talking about traveling to Disney with the girls, with my daughter too, and look what's happened.'

Roman also shared a letter on social media in tribute to De Miguel, reflecting on their friendship and stating he had 'brought happiness to everyone'.

'My friend... I can’t believe you’re gone... you have no idea how much I’m going to miss you. I didn’t just consider you a friend; I considered you a member of my own family,' Roman wrote.

'You were always there to help me when I was struggling—you were by my side during my worst moments.

'Many people didn’t truly know you, but having known you, I can say you were one of the best people I’ve ever had in my life: humble, hardworking, never one to look for trouble. You brought happiness to everyone around you, and above all, you were a truly good person.

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

De Miguel was stretchered off the field following the collision with Owono

'All the moments we shared keep coming to mind... that trip to Punta Cana with the four of us - a trip I will never forget... all the lunches and dinners we enjoyed together, the time we spent with our daughters, the escape rooms we both loved so much...

'Tamara and I are absolutely devastated right now, but we know that from up above, you’ll still be with us—and, most importantly, with your daughter, with María, and with your entire family.

'My friend, I’m going to miss you so much... I love you dearly! REST IN PEACE!!'

Confirming receipt of the preliminary autopsy report yesterday and the authorisation of the transfer of the footballer's body, the Canary Islands High Court of Justice said: 'The court investigating the footballer's death, which is Court of Investigation Number Two of the Santa Cruz de Tenerife Court of First Instance, received the preliminary autopsy report today.

'The court has authorized the transport of the young man's remains to the mainland for burial.'

Police investigating De Miguel's death are probing the emergency medical response as well as the possibility rival goalie Jesus Owono's horror tackle could be involuntary manslaughter.

It emerged on Tuesday that homicide squad officers based in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz had launched a probe as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation.

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono because the clash occurred during open play, although he is expected to be hit with a lengthy ban.

The goalkeeper shared a statement on Wednesday, revealing he is in 'enormous pain' over the death of De Miguel.

Owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesús.'

Thirty-year-old father-of-one De Miguel died on Tuesday morning at Nuestra Senora Candelaria University Hospital after his second-division club revealed his neurological condition had worsened.

Medical personnel involved in the footballer's care are expected to be questioned and detectives will sift through medical reports as part of the probe.

Police investigating the death of CD Tenerife footballer Jesus De Miguel are probing the emergency medical response

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono

Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who has lived in Spain since he was eight, was red-carded for kneeing Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel in the chest near the halfway line late into stoppage time. The match was suspended when the two sides were drawing 2-2.

De Miguel, whose partner Maria and one-year-old daughter Carla were watching from the stands, was reportedly revived by paramedics on the pitch after going into cardiac arrest before being rushed to hospital.

His club confirmed around 9.30am local time yesterday morning he had died at a hospital in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz about 8am, saying they were 'heartbroken' and had a 'lump in their throats'.

It said in a statement, after revealing earlier the footballer's neurological condition had worsened: 'Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats, and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, which occurred this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8am.

'There are no words of comfort, there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this profound sense of sorrow.

'We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones, and the entire 'tinerfeñismo' community, who today mourn this cruel outcome.

Owono is reportedly seeking to apologise to De Miguel's family before making any kind of public statement.

FC Andorra, reacting to news of the Tenerife striker's death in hospital, said yesterday morning: 'Heartbroken and devastated, we wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife.

By Darren Plant | 08 Nov 2026 15:20, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 15:31

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has recalled Youri Tielemans for Sunday's Premier League fixture against Aston Villa.

With the former Villa midfielder having replaced the injured Carlos Baleba during the early stages of the second half against Roma, the Belgian has been rewarded with an opportunity against Unai Emery's side.

#1871. Michael Carrick sends new message to Manchester United fans over Diogo Dalot boos

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has urged supporters “to be careful” with their boos after targeting Diogo Dalot during the Red Devils’ 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday.

Man Utd fans watched on at Old Trafford as their side twice rallied back from a two-goal deficit in dramatic fashion, eventually sharing a point with Unai Emery’s visitors.

For much of this season, Dalot has been deployed outside of his favoured position of right-back, instead lining up on the left in the absence of Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu.

Dorgu has recently returned to enough fitness to be named in matchday squads, and when the Danish wing-back was brought on to replace Dalot on 66 minutes on Sunday, boos rang around Old Trafford aimed at the Portuguese defender.

A regular starter in an often-criticised defence, Dalot had given away a penalty right at the start of the second half, allowing Aston Villa to regain their lead.

Under-pressure United boss Carrick was quick to defend his player, however.

Asked about the fans’ booing towards Dalot, Carrick responded: "We've got to be careful with that, I think.

"I understand the frustration, I understand the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it. We're all frustrated, we're all disappointed, and the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

"Diogo, he gives absolutely everything. He's played in different positions, he's played left-back, he's played really well at times. He gives a penalty away today.

“Maybe he can do a little bit better, all right, that's part of it, he's made a mistake, but he cares an awful lot and he's giving everything.

"So I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we've got.

“Picking a team and who plays the next game, that's a whole different decision, but it's a whole different game that we've got to look forward to now."

#1870. Romano: Milan remain obsessed with Inacio but Fonseca’s arrival could change things

It’s no secret that AC Milan will sign a defender in January, and one name is sitting firmly in the lead but he’s not alone.

Since the summer, Milan have been obsessed with the idea of signing Goncalo Inacio. His name was constant through the mercato and on deadline day, the Rossoneri tried to pounce on a last-minute deal. However, it was unsuccessful, understandably.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Within days of the mercato shutting, the Rossoneri were linked with another move in the January window and these suggestions have not gone away in the months since. Other names have been suggested, but again, Inacio remains the priority.

Speaking on his YouTube channel today, Fabrizio Romano offered an update on the club’s pursuit for Inacio ahead of the January mercato, via MilanNews.

“A defender will definitely arrive. He was supposed to arrive in the summer; he will arrive in January, so it’s no mystery. Milan also persistently sought him during the summer transfer window, an extra defender obviously in addition to Mario Gila, who was also an excellent investment by Milan, so the idea is to bring in at least another one.

“Milan reinstated Tomori a minute after the end of the summer transfer window out of necessity, but Milan’s idea is to take an extra defender. So a defender will definitely arrive.

“The name of Gonçalo Inácio must always be kept there because it is a name that has been in Milan’s mind since the first day of the summer transfer window; from when Ruben Amorim arrived until the last minute of the transfer window, he has always been in the thoughts anyway. There have been different attempts with different formulas.

“Milan had even considered, at a certain point at the end of August, a possible very expensive loan with an option to buy, so several solutions were considered that Sporting did not accept.

“Among other things, Sporting has changed its skin; Paolo Fonseca arrived on the bench, so we’ll see how much this will impact the dynamics of this operation. Clearly he’s not the only name, but Inacio is certainly a very welcome player; Milan has excellent relations with his agents, who are the same as Amorim.

“But I repeat, it doesn’t end here; there’s a list and Milan will make their choices.”

It’s a positive start that a defender will ‘definitely’ arrive; it’s just a case of whether they’re the right man now with Inacio not seeming like the definitive candidate.
