#1869. ‘Time passes by’ – Mancini warns Zaniolo he must seize Italy chance

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Roberto Mancini has warned Nicolo Zaniolo that he must start taking his opportunities to impress for Italy, before time runs out for the playmaker.

Zaniolo has been included in the Azzurri's squad for their upcoming Nations League fixtures against France and Belgium, with their qualification from Group A1 still in the balance.

Having taken seven points from their opening four games, Italy sit second in the group, three points below France and one above Belgium, meaning their matchday six meeting with the Red Devils – in Brussels on Sunday – could be a winner-take-all clash.

Zaniolo was initially included in Mancini's first squad since returning to the Italy job in September, but a thigh issue caused the Udinese man to pull out.

The 27-year-old also struggled with a hamstring problem at the start of the campaign, restricting him to just six Serie A appearances in 2026-27.

He has scored one goal and provided one assist this season for Udinese, who he joined on loan last season before making his stay permanent in the summer, and it has been more than two years since he represented his country.

Once seen as a burgeoning talent for Roma and Italy, Zaniolo has only won 19 senior caps – 10 of which have come from the bench – with the most recent of those coming against Ecuador in March 2024.

Zaniolo's only two senior international goals came against Armenia in November 2019, and Mancini has warned he will not get many more chances to shine on the big stage.

"I expect the same thing as I do from everyone else – to perform well and be consistent," Mancini told reporters, when asked what he expected from Zaniolo.

"He must start being decisive, because time passes by. He used to be a kid, and now he should be a player who makes a difference for the national team."

"Back in 2018, we had more experienced players," he said.

"Giorgio [Chiellini], Leo [Bonucci], [Marco] Verratti, Jorginho… they were the most experienced ones. Today, we don't have many."

San Siro will be the venue for Italy's meeting with France on Thursday, with Les Bleus knowing a victory would secure top spot in the group.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Saliba had been out since the World Cup semi-finals in the summer but he is now closing in on a return to first-team action.

He made Arsenal’s matchday squad against Slavia Prague in the Champions League last week, though manager Mikel Arteta then opted against having Saliba involved against Hull in the Premier League on Saturday.

It was decided that minutes for the U21s would be more beneficial and Saliba - who was not named in the latest France squad by Zinedine Zidane - started alongside captain Marli Salmon in a 5-2 Premier League 2 win over Villa at Boreham Wood’s Meadow Park.

Max Dowman - who is serving a three-match suspension at senior level after his sending off in the shock Carabao Cup defeat by Fleetwood last month - was among the scorers as he starred in a playmaker role.

Saliba was replaced at half-time but Arsenal’s U21s head coach David Horseman confirmed that was always the intention.

“He’s fine, by the way, it was all pre-planned, so nobody needs to panic,” Horseman said.

Saliba was at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday to watch Arsenal beat Hull 1-0 and extend their lead at the top of the Premier League table to five points.

He then joined up with the U21s on Sunday morning and impressed Horseman with his attitude and impact on the young group.

“Just the way he was in the meeting, everything about him, the way he prepares on the bus, the lads probably won’t notice it, but they should,” Horseman said.

#1866. Tottenham told Jayden Bogle red card verdict after official complaint in latest review

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham can feel hard done by by the decision not to send Jayden Bogle off for his tackle on Mathys Tel over the weekend.

The Leeds defender lunged in on the Frenchman during the Whites’ 1-0 win over Spurs at Elland Road, and the challenge left the forward in agony on the turf.

He was spotted in crutches after the game, with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi fearing the worst for the winger on the injury front.

Tel was forced off immediately, replaced by Dominic Solanke on 42 minutes.

Tottenham filed an official complaint to the refereeing body Pro Ref after the match, incensed at the lack of a red card, despite there being a pitchside VAR review by match official John Brooks in Yorkshire.

On Sky Sports’ ‘Ref Watch’ programme, former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher admitted that Bogle was very fortunate to stay on the pitch following the incident.

“He is extremely lucky, he catches him across the Achilles, high, we have this directive of 'above the ankle, or Achilles' and that falls under that line.

“We saw it with Ryan Sessegnon a few weeks ago with a similar tackle and [Jean-Philippe] Mateta last week.”

Former Spurs manager Tim Sherwood said that he “would not have been surprised” to see the right-back dismissed, while ex-Premier League striker Jay Bothroyd claimed that the tackle was “accidental” and that he did “not want to see red cards for those kinds of challenges”.

#1864. Roy Keane fires Michael Carrick warning after Manchester United chaos as huge call looms

Roy Keane has likened under-fire Manchester United manager Michael Carrick to a “politician”, claiming that he “talks a lot but doesn’t say much”.

Man Utd head into the November international break sat in the Premier League relegation zone despite twice recovering from a two-goal deficit to record a dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Given a reprieve ahead of the 1-0 defeat by Chelsea the weekend prior, Carrick oversaw a first win in 10 games across all competitions last Tuesday, when his struggling side came from 2-0 down to defeat depleted Roma 3-2 in the Champions League.

But despite the two comebacks at Old Trafford, Carrick’s job remains firmly in question - with Keane doubting his ability to turn things around.

Already out of the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle and sitting on just one win in the Premier League, Keane believes that Carrick is running out of time to find improvements.

Speaking on Sky Sports, he said: “It’s obviously difficult for the manager. Under pressure, no doubt. He talks a lot but doesn’t say much. I don’t know if that’s a tactic. Like a politician.

“He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there’s things we need to work on.

“But they better get moving on that. It’s the worst start in how many years, all these stats aren’t very good. If you keep giving up goals and chances, it’s just going to continue.

“What are we expecting to change over the next few weeks and months? What are they working on? They need to do a lot better than that.”

Following United’s 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth last month, fans directed their boos towards the players, owners and directors, while showing their support for Carrick.

In recent weeks many supporters have questioned the players’ desire, but Keane believes the latest performances show the squad’s resolve.

So, Amorim may now be reluctant to rotate as heavily, but that brings up new issues. If they keep going at this rate, they’ll head off track.

#1862. Barcelona and Spain defender Cubarsi wins Golden Boy award

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Barcelona and Spain centre-back Pau Cubarsi has been announced as the winner of the 2026 Golden Boy award.

The prize, which is handed to the best performer playing in European football under the age of 21, has now been won by four Barca players in the last six years.

Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal collected the prize in 2021, 2022 and 2024, respectively, and it cannot be awarded twice to the same player.

Paris Saint-Germain's Desire Doue scooped the award in 2025, while Kylian Mbappe (2017), Erling Haaland (2020) and Jude Bellingham (2023) are among the other recent winners.

Cubarsi is the first defender to land the award since Matthijs de Light in 2018, after he helped Barca defend their LaLiga title and Spain win the World Cup for the second time.

𝗣𝗔𝗨 𝗖𝗨𝗕𝗔𝗥𝗦𝗜, 𝗚𝗢𝗟𝗗𝗘𝗡 𝗕𝗢𝗬 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 https://t.co/y4LljnnhOg

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 9, 2026

The 19-year-old was also named the Young Player of the Tournament at the World Cup and finished 12th in the Ballon d'Or voting, as one of six Spain players to make the top 20.

Cubarsi led all players in the final for touches (139), successful passes (121), passing accuracy (96%), line-breaking passes (21) and clearances (six) in July's World Cup final, as La Roja beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time, thanks to Ferran Torres' goal.

There are only three instances on record (since 1966) of a player completing 100+ passes in a World Cup final. Cubarsi and his team-mate Rodri (101) are two of those, with Dunga the other, in Brazil's win over Italy in 1994 (130).

Cubarsi was one of two teenagers to start the showpiece match, alongside Yamal, as Spain became the first team to ever start multiple teenagers in a World Cup final.

Five players have now won the Golden Boy award while representing Barca, moving them further clear of Borussia Dortmund and Manchester United (three each) as the club with the most recipients.

Cubarsi has been named in Luis de la Fuente's latest squad, as Spain look to round off their Group A3 campaign with a perfect record, facing Czechia on Thursday and then England three days later.

#1861. Sunday's Premier League results: Brilliant Brighton climb to second as Chelsea suffer shock Sunderland loss

By Ellis Stevens | 08 Nov 2026 16:08, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 20:46

The Premier League's 10th matchday delivered another afternoon of exciting action on Sunday, with four fixtures taking place ahead of the final game between Manchester United and Aston Villa before the November international break.

Two of the division's so-called 'Bermuda Triangle' went head-to-head as Brighton & Hove Albion hosted Brentford, while the third member of the group, Bournemouth, travelled to face Ipswich Town.

Elsewhere, Premier League heavyweights Liverpool and Chelsea were also in action, facing up against Crystal Palace and Sunderland respectively.

Here, Sports Mole provides a roundup of Sunday's Premier League action.

"No goalkeeper is saving that!" Pascal Groß fires a penalty into the top corner to double Brighton's lead ? https://t.co/yARFiu19LL

Brighton & Hove Albion defeated fellow 'Bermuda Triangle' member Brentford 2-0 at the Amex Stadium, seeing the Seagulls climb to second in the Premier League standings.

Fabian Hurzeler's men have been one of the most impressive teams in the league this season, especially at home, where they remain unbeaten, and today's result marked their fourth win and fourth clean sheet in five home league fixtures.

Not only have Brighton's results impressed, but the Seagulls have had a knack for scoring screamers this season, and Diego Gomez added yet another wondergoal to his collection early in the match.

The midfielder sensationally picked out the top left corner with his weak foot just 15 minutes in, with Brighton boosted further by Igor Thiago's subsequent red card and Pascal Gross's emphatic finish from the spot.

Brighton continued to dominate and looked comfortable defensively, ultimately keeping their fourth home clean sheet and seventh of the season - just three less than they managed in the entirety of the 2025-26 Premier League campaign.

The victory lifts Hurzeler's side to second in the Premier League standings going into the November international break, while Brentford slide to eighth in the table after their second defeat of the term.

Enzo Le Fee dispatches the penalty as Sunderland take the lead against Chelsea! ?⚪️ https://t.co/cCtYsHVWB9

Sunderland secured a superb 1-0 victory against Chelsea at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats were the far more offensively dangerous side throughout the 90 minutes, but Enzo Le Fee's 36th-minute goal from the spot proved the only difference as Sunderland eventually claimed all three points.

Regis Le Bris' side, as a result, climbed away from the bottom of the Premier League table to 18th thanks to securing just their second win of the 2026-27 league season.

Chelsea, meanwhile, suffered their fourth defeat in the Premier League and dropped out of the Champions League places to fifth in the standings, with Xabi Alonso's side handed their second loss in the space of three league games.

Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz combine to put Liverpool 2-0 up! ? https://t.co/F6sw33FkYZ

Liverpool returned to winning ways with a 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park, ensuring Andoni Iraola's side avoided suffering a third straight defeat across all competitions.

The Reds have been winless inside 90 minutes in their last three matches, with a draw against Chelsea in the EFL Cup - which they did win on penalties - and losses to Arsenal and Fenerbahce in the Premier League and Champions League respectively.

However, Alexis Mac Allister's first-half header, Florian Wirtz's second-half strike and Alexander Isak's late finish sealed a streak-snapping victory for Liverpool, with Eddie Nketiah's late goal only a consolation for the Eagles, who were handed their seventh defeat of the Premier League campaign.

While Iraola's side now head into the international break in good spirits, as they climbed to fourth in the table after today's win, Pierre Sage goes into the November hiatus under increasing pressure.

The Crystal Palace boss has recorded just two wins and one draw in 10 league fixtures, with seven points after 10 games leaving the Eagles at the bottom of the standings.

What a start to the second half for Bournemouth! ? Ryan Christie's strike deflects off Leif Davis to double the Cherries' lead https://t.co/qSxUMe0wjD

Bournemouth defeated Ipswich Town 2-1 at Portman Road Stadium, extending their winning run to eight consecutive matches across all competitions.

Marco Rose, who won just two of his first eight matches at the helm, has overseen an incredible improvement over the past weeks, including leading the Cherries up to seventh after their fourth straight Premier League triumph.

The Cherries flew out from the blocks as Evanilson opened the scoring inside five minutes, meaning the striker has now scored in each of his last five Premier League appearances.

Ipswich were once again undone swiftly after kick-off in the second half, as Ryan Christie's effort deflected off Leif Davis and into the back of the net, doubling Bournemouth's lead.

However, the Jack Clarke pulled one back for the Tractor Boys from the penalty spot with 17 minutes to play, making for a nervy ending to the match, but the Cherries were able to cling onto the victory.

Bournemouth, as a result of the win, climbed to seventh in the table with 15 points, just three points outside the top four, while Ipswich remain 14th with 11 points.

#1860. Cristiano Ronaldo QUITS international football after explosive fall-out with Portugal manager: Superstar, 41, announces retirement in emotional five-minute video

Published: 05:34 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 10:58 EST, 5 November 2026

Cristiano Ronaldo has called time on his illustrious career in international football.

Ronaldo, 41, scored a world record 146 goals in 234 games for Portugal and won the 2016 European Championship as well as two Nations League titles.

His retirement comes just weeks after his explosive falling-out with new manager Jorge Jesus, which ended with Ronaldo abandoning Portugal's camp during the most recent international break in September and October.

It appeared as if he could return for the upcoming break this month for clashes with Denmark and Wales, but he has decided to step away after 23 years.

In his retirement statement, he admitted that he had at times 'failed' and revealed that his decision was difficult, but felt proud of his work and willing to hand over the number seven jersey.

The Al-Nassr star is hoping to pass the baton to his son, 16-year-old Cristiano Junior, who this week has been called up for Portugal's Under-17s.

Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 aged 18 and went on to play in six World Cups, a record he shares with Lionel Messi, as well as six European Championships, two Nations League finals, and a Confederations Cup.

Cristiano Ronaldo has called time on his illustrious international career with Portugal

The highlight of his Portugal career was lifting the 2016 European Championship, even if he got injured in the final

He never reached a World Cup final and cried after Portugal were knocked out by Spain in the last 16 over the summer

Ironically, his most memorable hour in a Portugal shirt was arguably when he wasn't playing. After getting injured during the 2016 Euros final, he cut such a passionate figure on the touchline, barking instructions to his team-mates, that he had practically taken over from manager Fernando Santos.

However, his dream of winning a World Cup always eluded him, and his best results were reaching the semi-finals in 2006 in Germany and the quarters in 2022 in Qatar.

His final act in football's greatest tournament was Portugal's 1-0 defeat by arch-rivals Spain at this summer's World Cup – a devastating day which saw him leave in tears.

And his final minutes in a Portugal shirt came against Wales in September, when he played 67 minutes in a 1-0 Nations League win over Wales.

After being left on the bench for their subsequent match against Norway, Ronaldo had a row with manager Jesus and flew away from Portugal's camp via his private jet.

Marking his retirement, he wrote: 'To the people of Portugal, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of our national team. I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility to wear it, to defend it, and to take it with me to stadiums all over the world.

'Today has come the moment to hand it over to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made just with the head, they are also made with the heart.

'I was always demanding of myself. I always wanted more, I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this jersey. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories I will never forget.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner admitted he had at times 'failed' but was still proud

His time with Portugal in the last international break ended acrimoniously as he abandoned their camp after being left on the bench against Norway

Manager Jorge Jesus insisted that Ronaldo is welcome back, and did his team-mates

'There were defeats that even today I find hard to remember. I also failed, I also suffered, there were also moments when I was not able to give the Portuguese people what they so desired. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

'Throughout these years, I learned very simple things. Goals pass, trophies stay in museums, records end up being broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we occupy in people's hearts.

'If I ever made you happy, if ever a goal of mine made you hug someone, forget a problem, or simply feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also that. We suffer together, we get up together.

'If I got this far, it was because we were always hand in hand. And to the Portuguese, to all Portuguese people scattered around the world, I want to tell you one last thing. There is an image I will always carry with me: the moment the national anthem begins. I look around, I see my teammates, I see the stands, I see children, mothers, fathers, and grandfathers, I see Portuguese people who came from so far just to be there.

'And during those minutes, we stop being different. There are no clubs, there are no colors, there are no classes, there are no professions, there are no opinions. There is only one passion: Portugal.'

There will be questions over the way Ronaldo's international career has ended – to the public, it appears to be on rather bitter terms.

Ronaldo was livid after being left on the bench despite warming-up for Portugal's Nations League win over Norway on September 27 – the first time he has been an unused substitute during his 18-year international career.

That led to him skipping three training sessions and abandoning the camp for Portugal's last two matches of the international break, fleeing to Spain via private jet.

The 41-year-old has scored scored 146 goals in 234 games - the most of anybody ever

He did not even watch their next match against Norway because he was soaring away on his plane with his family.

The former Manchester United star was vexed at how Jesus had handled his press conference after leaving him on the bench.

Ronaldo insisted that Jesus had broken a promise to apologise to the 'Portuguese people' and his team-mates for not bringing him on.

He claimed he had been guaranteed 30 minutes of football against Norway after the Portuguese FA persuaded him not to retire following the World Cup.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner even offered to retire if that was what the coach and head of Portuguese FA wanted, only for them to reiterate their desire to have him.

But most hurtfully, Ronaldo released a stinging 1,996-word statement accusing Jesus of 'broken promises'. He said the manager had agreed to deliver an eight-point mea culpa taking responsibility for leaving him on the bench after a supposed pact to play him.

Jesus did concede it was a mistake to make him warm up but gave a different narrative of events, saying: 'The match in Norway was not part of the plan I drew up for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed.'

In the end, Ronaldo was fined £215 by the Portuguese FA and technically banned for a month – though that was backdated, making him free for their upcoming fixtures.

It was a messy episode – not unlike how he left Manchester United for a second time in 2022 – and the question remains as to whether he would have still been playing had the row never occurred.

'To the people of Portugal, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of our national team. I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility to wear it, to defend it, and to take it with me to stadiums all over the world.

'Today has come the moment to hand it over to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made just with the head, they are also made with the heart.

'A journey comes to an end that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever. When I look back and think about everything I experienced in the national team, I do not just see games, goals, records, or trophies. I see people. I see immigrants who, for 90 minutes, felt Portugal a little closer.

'I see millions of Portuguese people that I never met personally, but who were part of my life. Because at the end of everything, football is much greater than a game. Football is people. Throughout my career in the national team, I sought to surpass my limits. I wanted to win, I wanted to be the best, I wanted to make history.

'I was always demanding of myself. I always wanted more, I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this jersey. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories I will never forget.

'There were defeats that even today I find hard to remember. I also failed, I also suffered, there were also moments when I was not able to give the Portuguese people what they so desired. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

'Throughout these years, I learned very simple things. Goals pass, trophies stay in museums, records end up being broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we occupy in people's hearts.

'If I ever made you happy, if ever a goal of mine made you hug someone, forget a problem, or simply feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also that. We suffer together, we get up together.

'We believe again. Portugal will always need youngsters who dream of it, players who never give up, new generations who believe it is possible to reach where no one has reached. Because a country that continues to create new heroes is a country that never stops believing in itself.

'To my national team teammates, I want to leave a special word. Thank you for every run, for every hug, for every argument, for every silence before entering the pitch. For every victory we celebrated together and for every defeat that made us stronger. I had the privilege of being your captain, but no captain walks alone. And you are part of my history. To all the coaches, directors, doctors, physiotherapists, kit men, staff, and so many people who worked with me over these years, my thank you.

'Many of you never appeared in these photographs. But without you, none of those photographs would have been possible. To my family, thank you for sharing this dream with me. Thank you for understanding the absences, the sacrifices, and the moments when the national team had to occupy a space that also belonged to you.

'If I got this far, it was because we were always hand in hand. And to the Portuguese, to all Portuguese people scattered around the world, I want to tell you one last thing. There is an image I will always carry with me: the moment the national anthem begins. I look around, I see my teammates, I see the stands, I see children, mothers, fathers, and grandfathers, I see Portuguese people who came from so far just to be there.

'And during those minutes, we stop being different. There are no clubs, there are no colors, there are no classes, there are no professions, there are no opinions. There is only one passion: Portugal.

'That is a feeling I will carry with me for the rest of my life. Today, my journey on the pitch with the national team ends. I leave with my head held high, proud of the path I walked and with the awareness that I gave everything I had for Portugal.

'But I will never stop being one of you. I will continue to suffer, to cheer, and to celebrate every victory of Portugal. I spent my life working to be the best player in the world. Today I realize that the greatest victory was having deserved to represent the best country in the world.

'Thank you for these 23 years. Thank you for believing in me. Thank you for allowing me to live a dream that began when I was just a boy in Madeira, chasing a ball. The number seven jersey stays, the pride of having worn it will be mine forever. Portugal will always be in me. Farewell always, Cristiano Ronaldo.'

#1859. Alisson reveals transfer plan with Liverpool contract set to expire

Alisson Becker has revealed that he wants to stay at Liverpool, despite his contract on Merseyside expiring this summer.

The Brazilian has been with the Anfield club since 2018, when he moved from Roma for £66.8million, making him the most expensive goalkeeper ever before Chelsea moved to land Kepa Arrizabalaga from Athletic Club.

The 34-year-old has been the Reds’ go-to No1 since his arrival, and he has played under three managers in his time there.

Jurgen Klopp was the head coach that signed him, and he retained his place under Arne Slot and now Andoni Iraola, despite the arrival of Giorgi Mamardashvili from Valencia.

Questions have been raised over whether Alisson will remain a Liverpool player beyond this season, with no news of a contract extension as of yet.

His current deal runs out at the end of the current campaign, but the shot-stopper wants to stay put.

"Yes, in my mind," he told reporters. "I’m focused on playing every game but in my mind I’m happy to stay. You know, that depends on a lot of aspects and different situations.

"But my will is to stay. I’m happy here, my family is happy here. I’m still hungry for titles and for delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can. So that’s my thinking on that."

Alisson played a key role in the Reds’ 3-1 win at Crystal Palace at the weekend, a result that sees Iraola’s men up to fourth in the Premier League table, and pushes Palace boss Pierre Sage closer to the sack.

#1857. Arsenal sent clear new penalty verdict in call for law change

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal were denied a penalty against Hull after the officials incorrectly applied the laws of the game.

That is the view of former referee Dermot Gallagher, who said of the incident: “ethically it is right but by the laws it is wrong”.

The Gunners beat Hull 1-0 on Saturday thanks to Martin Odegaard’s second-half goal and will spend the international break sitting five points clear at the top of the Premier League.

However, there was a controversial moment in the first half at the Emirates Stadium when the score remained 0-0 and Arsenal were not awarded a penalty.

Referee Farai Hallam stopped play to go to the monitor and assess whether Nobel Mendy’s pull of Kai Havertz’s shirt in the box was a foul.

It was decided that while Havertz was fouled and the contact was worthy of a penalty, the Arsenal striker was offside and so a free-kick was given to Hull.

That went against the laws of the game, which say the offside should have been irrelevant as Havertz was not attempting to play the ball or challenging an opponent for it.

Gallagher believes that Arsenal should have been awarded a spot-kick, but expressed sympathy for the officials involved.

He claimed that “common sense” would suggest that Havertz was offside and so a penalty could not be awarded, as he called for the rules to be tweaked to avoid such confusion.

“The law says that if a player in an offside position is fouled before the offside occurs, a foul should be given and therefore a penalty,” Gallagher said on Sky Sports.

“In law, you should give a penalty. It is quite clear, the foul occurred before. But we talk about common sense. Havertz is 100 per cent offside. His starting position is offside.

“Three things he can’t do: he can’t play the ball as he’d be interfering, he can’t challenge an opponent and he can’t go in front of the goalkeeper. He is offside and the net result should be a penalty.

“Common sense is not allowed. When you think of it morally, can you really give a penalty for a player who is never in an onside position? He can’t play the ball.

“The process of VAR was fantastic. The assistant calls offside the minute the ball comes in. The start position for the assistant was always offside.

“Ethically it is right but by law it is wrong. There is scope for tightening it up [the laws].”

#1856. Stevenage vs Fulham Under-21s - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 08 Nov 2026 16:15

Stevenage and Fulham Under-21s square off on Tuesday night, with both teams already aware of whether they will feature in the EFL Trophy knockout stages.

While Stevenage sit top of Group B in the Southern section with successive wins and have secured their progress, the young Cottagers are already eliminated after back-to-back defeats.

Having failed with a surprise bid for promotion in 2025-26, Alex Revell will be disappointed that his Stevenage outfit are down in 16th position in the League One table.

However, a 2-2 draw at Leicester City in their last third tier outing was followed by an outstanding 1-0 triumph at Oxford United in the FA Cup first round.

Carl Piergianni's fourth-minute goal earned Revell's side one of the most notable victories of the weekend, and it keeps them interested in two different cup competitions for the foreseeable future.

In the EFL Trophy, Stevenage have already thrashed Walsall by a 6-1 scoreline and edged out Leicester by the odd goal in three on home territory.

Stevenage now have five wins and one draw from their last eight matches in all competitions, with a further notable success over Plymouth Argyle included in that run.

Meanwhile, Fulham Under-21s have conceded nine goals in their defeats to Leicester and Walsall.

The Foxes cruised to a 6-1 win when welcoming the young Cottagers to the King Power Stadium, before the Saddlers came through by a 3-2 scoreline.

Fulham Under-21s also suffered defeat to Worthing in the National League Cup on November 3, further highlighting their struggles against senior opposition.

On a more positive note, they did register a 4-1 win at Stoke City in their last Premier League 2 fixture, leaving them in fourth spot behind Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea.

Fulham Under-21s form (all competitions):

Daniel Barden, Alfie Thornett, Terry Taylor, Matt Smith, Chem Campbell and Michael Mellon could all be drafted into the Stevenage XI.

Revell may also look to introduce at least one youngster into the starting lineup as he bids to rest as many senior players as possible.

Tommy Setford, Brian Broggio and Josh Magennis are all on international duty.

Barring any such selections, Fulham Under-21s may line up similar to the recent win over Stoke Under-21s.

In his first appearance of the season, Terrell Works scored a double, and the attacker should feature again after that 58-minute outing.

Barden; Vancooten, Casey, Thornett, Earley; Sanderson, Taylor, Smith, Campbell; Turhan, Mellon

Fulham Under-21s possible starting lineup:

Allen; Cooke, Gomins, Slade, White; Nwoko, Chingwaro; Zepa, Casey, Works, Sani

With Stevenage likely to rotate as much as regulations allow, Fulham may feel that there is an opportunity for a win. However, the young Cottagers already conceding nine goals leads up to predict a relatively comfortable victory for the home side.

#1855. Josh King: Fulham star reveals England mentor after shock Nations League call-up by Thomas Tuchel

Fulham’s Josh King has revealed that Jude Bellingham has taken him under his wing for England, and insists he is willing to play wherever Thomas Tuchel needs him.

The attacking midfielder was called up to take part in the Three Lions’ pre-World Cup training camp in Florida in June but on Friday received his first proper call-up to the senior squad ahead of Nations League matches against Croatia on Thursday and Spain on Sunday.

While only 19, King has been given plenty of responsibility for his club under Alvaro Arbeloa this season and has been rewarded now with the chance to earn his senior international debut over the coming week.

“There were a lot of people I learned from [in the pre-World Cup camp].” King said.

“Jude was a big person for me. He took me under his wing and tried to make me feel welcome. There were a lot of players like that. Harry Kane as well, he was one person who really made me feel welcome and tried to help me through my time there.

“But it's a credit to what England have going here, everyone is a really good person as well as good player on the pitch.”

King added: “Playing for England is the dream so to be that one step closer is an amazing achievement, something I've been working towards for a long time. I'm grateful to the manager for putting his trust in me.”

Tuchel said on Friday that he had King as one of his options on the right wing this month, but sees him as able to play in a variety of attacking positions.

“I'm happy to play anywhere for the manager,” King said on Monday. “I have to add other parts to my game, in wider positions you might have to cover defensively or make runs in behind.

“I'm capable of playing lots of different positions, which is probably one of the reasons why I'm here.”

In an interview with Standard Sport in April, King said he wants to become “one of the best midfielders in the world” and dreams in time of being a “leader” for club and country.

#1854. Liverpool sent new Dominik Szoboszlai injury update as statement issued

Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai will be assessed on Monday to determine his fitness for international duty with Hungary.

Szoboszlai was forced off in the second half of the Reds’ 3-1 win at Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday due to a knee complaint.

During the last international break, Szoboszlai aggravated an existing muscular issue in his thigh, later breaking down just half an hour into his comeback against Brentford as he ended up missing five matches in total.

The latest issue has led to doubts over his availability to play for Hungary in their upcoming Nations League matches against Georgia and Northern Ireland.

The Hungarian Football Federation (MLSZ) released a statement on Monday which read: “(Dominik Szoboszlai) who was substituted in the 69th minute of Liverpool FC's match yesterday, is undergoing tests today, Monday, following the usual protocol in such cases. We will, of course, keep the public informed of developments as soon as possible."

Andoni Iraola admitted that Szoboszlai was not fully fit and hoped that Liverpool would not lose more key players to injury during the latest international break.

“Dom definitely wasn’t 100 per cent in the second half,” the Reds boss said after the win at Selhurst Park. "Let’s see. The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games.

"In the last international break we lost three very important players in Alex (Isak), Cody (Gakpo) and Dom. So now I'm praying - it's the last thing we need.”

Iraola offered insight into Szoboszlai’s latest issue, adding: “I think Dom extended the knee a little bit. It was fine but not 100 per cent. He has to be careful to see if he can play for the international team or not.

“I hope we are in a better place in two weeks. I know Dom will do everything to go as he loves to play for the national team, but he wasn’t 100 per cent when he finished the game.

#1853. AC Milan 0-2 Ferencvaros: Five things we learned – a poor squad picked apart

AC Milan’s Europa League misery continued at San Siro on Thursday night as they were beaten 2-0 by Ferencvaros.

Ruben Amorim made six changes to the team that won the derby against Inter, hoping that the entire group would remain buoyed by that performance to secure a much-needed win in Europe. However, what followed was the worst performance of his tenure so far.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Lenny Joseph netted twice in the second half to capitalise on errors and fire the Hungarian side to a memorable win. Ferencvaros were not even rocked by a red card to the substitute Yusuf as they kept the Rossoneri at bay quite easily, securing a two-goal win they deserved.

The result means that Milan have now dropped out of even the top 24 spots, and they can just about say goodbye to any hopes of direct last-16 qualification barring a miracle. Ivan Stoev has five things we learned from another dismal midweek game.

It’s difficult to pick five talking points after a game like this, as we can probably spend quite a bit of time discussing how bad each of the players were. But let’s try to address the bigger issue.

This squad is full of sheep, lacking both leaders and the quality to compete. We can talk all about how much Amorim rotates the squad and try to ease the blow by suggesting the Rossoneri didn’t field their best XI. Yet, if the management were serious about making the club competitive, then the rotational players should be above the quality of almost all teams competing in the Europa League, bar a few.

Obviously, if we assume Amorim is the right choice and Gerry Cardinale is serious, then it will take a lot more than a single transfer window and three new players to get Milan to compete on a few fronts, which was further proven against Ferencvaros.

Out of the whole squad, the only player that can change a game is Diego Moreira, who doesn’t play every game and has lots of room for improvement still. Not to mention that playing with the likes of Filippo Terracciano, Ardon Jashari and even Goncalo Ramos is not helping Belgium at all.

The rest of the squad lack either the quality or the mentality. The collective arrogance on the pitch was insufferable to watch, with Ferencvaros looking like the only side that had any desire to actually win. Whilst the Diavolo looked like they were playing a game in the park with no aggression, no focus, no intensity. No nothing.

It’s a bit pointless to discuss individuals because I think the wider point is clear – Milan lack leaders, Milan lack quality and Milan lack a game changer that can get the ball and make something happen when the tough gets going.

It was made evident after four games in the Europa League and a few blunders in Serie A that there’s lots of work to be done in January and next summer.

Again, it’s difficult to pick and choose which player to discuss, but given Ramos is the Rossoneri’s most expensive signing ever, it’s probably fair that the pressure starts mounting on him.

Listen, I wasn’t too bothered by the lack of goals initially, as the striker did well in the build-up and opened up space for his teammates; he also ran a lot in both phases of the game. Let’s also be honest, he has lacked the service to actually get the goal-scoring opportunities.

Nevertheless, in the last few games and especially against Ferencvaros, he has been dire – his build-up is poor, his ball control is pretty bad and when he does get a shot off, it’s usually miles away.

Now, obviously he’s not a striker that’s going to create chances for himself; he lacks the pace and the trickery, which is fine if you are good in the other aspects of the game. However, we can’t keep grasping for straws.

The reality is that the former PSG man is just not living up to the expectations given the hefty sum paid for him in the summer.

In retrospect, maybe it wasn’t wise to spend such a sum on a player who needs quality around him in order to be a better facilitator or to receive more chances overall. The reality as of now is that the Portuguese is a disappointment.

Again, as we said, most players in the squad lack quality or mentality and unfortunately for us there are some that lack both and it’s way past the tipping point at this stage.

Terracciano, for starters, has not shown anything worth mentioning in all of his games with the red and black shirt and there’s really no reason for him to get minutes. Even without pressure, he’s just not of the needed level.

Jashari is another one that the fans and the management have hoped will bounce back after his lengthy injury after joining Milan. Yet, he’s probably had one good game from start to finish and there’s always gaps in his game.

It’s probably wise at this point to accept he’s not going to live up to the expectations and a solution needs to be found on the market, especially given Luka Modric will most likely be retiring at the end of the season.

There are also other players in this category that didn’t necessarily participate in last night’s game but should have the same fate – Pervis Estupinan and Ruben Loftus-Cheek to name a couple.

If nothing else, these poor performances should highlight to the management where the gap in quality is and what the strategy on the transfer market should be.

4. De Winter’s disastrous performance proves costly

I think the biggest individual call-out should definitely be the Belgian, who played an awful back pass to Lorenzo Torriani on the first goal. Yes, the keeper could’ve and should’ve done much better, but that back pass was just so sloppy – it could put an outfield player in a tricky situation, let alone a goalkeeper that perhaps isn’t as comfortable with his feet.

This especially coming from a player who should’ve been a certainty at the back given the heavily rotated squad.

We can also partly criticise the intervention on the second goal, because it started the whole sequence leading to the Joseph’s brace. Yes, it was a bit unlucky where the ball ended up, but you can also argue it was sloppy, the same way you can argue that a keeper clearing the ball into the opponent’s feet after a shot instead of towards the corner is the keeper’s fault to an extent.

It’s just unacceptable to go from bullying Thuram to being bullied by not even Ferencvaros’s first-choice striker.

5. Amorim’s tactics fail, but the players also struggle

I think it’s probably fair to criticise the Portuguese coach a bit too, as the Hungarians totally outplayed the Diavolo at the San Siro and were tactically better. All in all, they had the answer to everything Milan tried to offer on the night.

At the same time, I’m torn to put the blame fully on Ruben Amorim because he did make a triple change at half-time, bringing on Pulisic, Moreira and Gila, which was still at 0-0. At that point, the Rossoneri had more than enough quality on the pitch to be able to deal with whatever Ferencvaros had to offer.

Instead, two individual mistakes gave away the opening goal and it all went downhill from there. Even after the red card, Milan struggled to create a big chance.

I personally struggle to blame this fully on tactics given all the circumstances and we are back to the point that the Milan squad are just not good enough and lacks that killer mentality.

#1852. Brighton 2-0 Brentford: Pascal Gross equals Mesut Ozil Premier League record

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 16:16, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 16:31

Brighton & Hove Albion playmaker Pascal Gross equalled a Premier League record set by Mesut Ozil in the Seagulls' 2-0 triumph over Brentford on Sunday afternoon.

Fabian Hurzeler's men enhanced their Premier League title credentials once again at the Amex Stadium, where first-half goals from Gross and Diego Gomez either side of Igor Thiago's red card did the damage.

After Gomez propelled Brighton into the ascendancy with just 15 minutes gone, Gross was given the chance to double the Seagulls' lead from the penalty spot thanks to Keane Lewis-Potter's challenge on Luka Vuskovic.

The veteran midfielder made no mistake with an incredible top-corner strike to rubber-stamp Brighton's victory, and in turn equal Ozil's record for the most combined Premier League goals and assists from a German player.

Gross has now had a direct hand 87 Premier League goals - 35 of his own and 52 assists - while Ozil managed 33 goals and 54 assists during his time in the top flight with Arsenal.

87 - Pascal Groß and Mesut Özil are now tied for the most goal involvements by ?? German players in the Premier League: Özil - 33 goals, 54 assists Groß - 35 goals, 52 assists Playmakers. https://t.co/hQxnGBczxO

The 35-year-old Gross has also had a direct hand in 10 goals in as many Premier League matches in the 2026-27 season, scoring four of his own while setting up six more for the Seagulls.

Already a fan favourite during his first stint at the Amex Stadium, Gross has been nothing short of a revelation for the Seagulls since returning from Borussia Dortmund in 2025 for a second stint on the South Coast.

Also now just one game away from reaching 300 in a Brighton kit, Gross will almost certainly break Ozil's record before the season is over, although he has a bit further to go to become the highest scoring German in Premier League history.

That record was broken just last week, as Arsenal's Kai Havertz scored his 46th Premier League goal against Liverpool, surpassing Ilkay Gundogan's previous best of 45 for Premier League Germans.

Nevertheless, Gross's 35 puts him third in the charts, while his next active closest challenger is Brentford's Kevin Schade, who has netted 24 goals in the English top flight.

Beating Arsenal at home, Manchester City away and slaying aside almost every other foe in their path, Brighton could do little more to cement their status as serious Premier League title challengers.

The Seagulls have now risen to second place in the Premier League table behind Arsenal, sitting five points adrift of the reigning champions and one clear of a struggling Manchester City side.

Furthermore, the Citizens' place in the top flight remains in major doubt as fans await the verdict of their appeal against 114 charges, while Liverpool and Chelsea have lacked consistency since the campaign began.

The sample size remains small, but after 10 matches, Brighton have shown every sign of lasting the course and pushing the holders all the way.

#1851. England XI vs Croatia: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Nations League

Dan Burn has been added to the England squad as a replacement for the injured Marc Guehi ahead of Thursday’s match against Croatia.

The Three Lions face Croatia at Wembley Stadium in their penultimate Nations League group game, before completing their group-phase in Madrid against world champions Spain on Sunday.

Manchester City centre-back Guehi was assessed over the weekend after being substituted with a hip injury at half time of their defeat to Nottingham Forest but has now pulled out of the squad.

In his place, Thomas Tuchel called up the 34-year-old Newcastle defender. He had said on Friday that “difficult phone calls” had been had with Burn, Dean Henderson and Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson when leaving them behind. But the former is now in as Guehi’s replacement.

Captain Harry Kane is expected to start and will overtake Peter Shilton to become England’s all-time most-capped player.

Arsenal duo Bukayo Saka (injury) and Noni Madueke (selection decision) are not in the squad this month but the head coach has explained that he sees his options on the right wing as being Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha, Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers, Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White and Fulham’s Josh King.

Declan Rice is back in the mix and available after missing the last international break due to load management.

Jobe Bellingham of Borussia Dortmund, brother of Real Madrid’s Jude, is in the squad for the very first time at senior level. He, King and the Brighton veteran goalkeeper Jason Steele are the only uncapped players among Tuchel’s squad.

The German is expected to go strong in both matches after revealing on Friday that it matters to him to push to finish top of their Nations League group despite currently trailing Spain by three points.

Tuchel has a choice to make between Jordan Pickford and James Trafford over to start as his goalkeeper. Both were handed two games each during the last extended international break.

#1850. Knee issue rules Yamal out of Spain-Czechia game

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Lamine Yamal will miss Spain's Nations League game against Czechia on Thursday due to a knee injury.

The Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) confirmed the winger's absence on Monday, after he sustained the knock during Barcelona's 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid the previous day.

Yamal still played the full 90 minutes as Hansi Flick's side recovered from a goal down to move three points clear at the top of LaLiga, assisting the second of Fermin Lopez's goals and creating seven chances in total.

He became the first Blaugrana player to reach that figure in a LaLiga match against Atleti since October 2008, when Xavi did so under Pep Guardiola.

Yamal has had an outstanding start to the season, registering 25 goal involvements in 16 games across all competitions (13 goals, 12 assists) – the most of any player from Europe's top five leagues.

Michael Olise (61) and Pascal Gross (57) are the only players to create more chances than Yamal's 54, while he has also attempted (118) and completed (65) the most dribbles.

He is one of only two players to already reach double figures for goals and assists this campaign, alongside Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane (10 goals, 11 assists).

In a statement, the RFEF said Yamal, David Raya and Mikel Oyarzabal were expected to join their team-mates in training later this week, while Liverpool's Victor Munoz has been handed a late call-up to Luis de la Fuente's group.

#1849. Next Crystal Palace manager: Contenders to replace Pierre Sage as clear favourite emerges

Pierre Sage will be sacked as Crystal Palace manager following Sunday’s 3-1 home defeat by Liverpool.

The Frenchman’s job has been under serious scrutiny for weeks now, with Palace heading into the November international break sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table after winning just two and losing seven of their first 10 games this season.

Sage has struggled to get his ideas across since taking over from Oliver Glasner in the summer, having enjoyed a terrific campaign with Lens last term.

The Eagles have the worst defence in the Premier League with 24 goals conceded so far, and Sage has run out of time to convince Palace’s decision-makers that he is the right man for the job.

With an announcement on Sage’s future imminent, they have already sounded out potential replacements.

Standard Sport has assessed who could take over at Selhurst Park next...

Out of work since being sacked by Tottenham in February, Thomas Frank was one of several candidates that Palace looked at to succeed Glasner in the summer and is the early frontrunner to replace Sage.

Crystal Palace set to sack Sage with club bottom of Premier League

Frank’s reputation is in need of rehabilitation, and it is unclear how much of a toll his torrid eight-month spell in charge of Spurs took, but he remains highly regarded after his work with Brentford.

Frank released a statement in June saying he was taking some time out of football before his next job, so the Dane may be unwilling to jump into a role so soon after the season has started.

Another manager who stepped away from football over the summer, Kieran McKenna made the shock decision to leave Ipswich after earning promotion back to the Premier League.

One of Britain’s most highly sought-after young coaches, McKenna’s decision to spend more time with his family came as a surprise, but potentially hints at the fact that he is not yet ready to get back into management.

McKenna’s patient, possession-based style would constitute a dramatic change in tactics for Palace, but the Northern Irishman is comfortable using a three-man defence when his team has the ball.

Bringing in former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe would be considered quite the coup for Palace.

The Englishman has attracted interest from Manchester United amid ongoing doubts over Michael Carrick’s future and guided Newcastle to Carabao Cup glory in 2025.

Howe is actively open to new opportunities, but is said to be willing to wait for an elite, high-profile job, which could leave Palace out of the running.

Arguably the most divisive name on the list, Sean Dyche’s pragmatic approach is a far cry from the expansive, counter-attacking football Palace fans have been used to under Glasner and, to a lesser extent, Sage.

Dyche’s Premier League experience, especially given that Palace will have one eye on ensuring they stay in the top-flight, makes him an attractive proposition for those in the boardroom.

Whether they would be prepared to face the inevitable backlash his appointment would prompt is a different question entirely, though.

Coventry boss Frank Lampard is reportedly under consideration for the Palace job despite signing only a new contract with the promoted Sky Blues in June.

Lampard is a long-standing target and one of several other candidates Palace are reportedly eyeing up alongside Kim Hellberg and Vitor Matos, who have led Middlesbrough and Swansea, respectively, towards the top of the Championship table this term.

Free agent Vitor Pereira is also said to be on Palace’s shortlist, while Australia head coach and former Palace captain Tony Popovic could be a surprise contender.

England assistant Anthony Barry is a risky but potentially intriguing appointment, while former Wolves boss Rob Edwards is well known to Palace sporting director Matt Hobbs.

#1845. GdS: €100m at risk for Milan between Champions and Europa League – the breakdown

The ups and downs that AC Milan have experienced so far this season could prove costly in the end, as highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning.

Ruben Amorim’s tenure at the club has certainly been a mixed bag so far. While the results in the league have been okay with 21 points after 10 games, they have been the opposite in the Europa League with a mere three points after four games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Gazzetta dello Sport reports this morning (see featured image), the problem isn’t just that Milan are struggling on the pitch, but also that it could have a massive effect on the finances. Between a top-four finish and a Europa League failure, we are talking about €100m.

Starting with the present, Milan have collected a mere €14.6m from the Europa League so far, excluding ticket sales for the games against Benfica and Ferencvaros. In other words, it’s just the guaranteed revenue plus the prize money for a win (€450k).

Direct qualification to the knockout phase, which was definitely the goal at the start, has now become rather difficult. Not even winning all of the remaining four games would be a guarantee, as that would take Milan to 15 points, and 16 might be required.

The feeling is that Milan have to focus on reaching the knockout play-offs instead. If they were to fail even with that, as the pink newspaper continues, we would be talking about a loss of €8m for the round of 16, between prize money and ticket sales.

Looking at the bigger picture, given that the Rossoneri among the favourites to win the competition in the summer, doing so would generate total revenue of €40m. Furthermore, lifting the trophy would secure qualification to the Champions League.

After missing the last two editions, failing to qualify yet again would be a massive failure for the entire RedBird project. This is especially true as the 2027-28 season will mark the beginning of a new cycle for UEFA in terms of commercial and TV rights, with numbers expected to significantly increase.

According to the newspaper, the total pot of prize money for the participating clubs will increase from the current €2.46bn to €2.8bn. For the Rossoneri, this would mean going from a minimum revenue of around €40m to around €50m, even before stepping onto the pitch.

To this figure, one must add around €10-15m from the ticket sales, so failure to qualify for the competition next season would mean missing out on a minimum of €60m (!). It could quickly rise to €70-80m too, so we really are talking about a lot.

Qualifying for the Champions League would increase the overall revenue by more than 20% and fuel Milan’s project of growth, especially since other improvements are on the cards too. For example, from 2028-39, Adidas will start paying €50m per season to the club.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Everton have won their last three games in all competitions, beating Newcastle United twice – in the EFL Cup and the Premier League – and Coventry City.

#1842. Tottenham seek ban on journalist over anti-Spurs chants with Arsenal fans

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham have lodged a formal complaint to the Premier League about the actions of a reporter working for ESPN Brasil.

Joao Castelo-Branco, who works as an English football correspondent for ESPN, was seen in video footage shared on his personal social media taking part in anti-Tottenham chanting with Arsenal fans in Sao Paulo.

The video was shared on Castelo-Branco’s personal Instagram page as well as an account belonging to an ESPN podcast and has now led to Spurs filing an official complaint against the journalist.

As part of their complaint, Tottenham have asked the Premier League to prevent Castelo-Branco from covering the club in future. That includes attending matches, press conferences and potential interviews.

The exclusions would not affect any other reporter or the broadcaster themselves, with ESPN a Premier League rights holder in the Caribbean and South America.

Castelo-Branco apologised for his actions in an interview with The Times and said the videos had since been removed from both social media accounts.

“I wanted to apologise to the club for the video I recorded with Arsenal fans in Brazil singing a derogatory chant about Tottenham Hotspur,” Castelo-Branco said. “Given my role as a correspondent in the UK, I feel I made a mistake.

“The video was posted on the podcast Instagram page and reproduced on my personal page. I understand it can be offensive to Spurs and Spurs fans and I should have thought more about singing that and the reach it could have.

“ESPN was notified by the Premier League about Tottenham seeing and disliking the post, and we agreed to delete it. Hopefully we can move on, and I will rethink and be more careful with the boundaries of having that persona on the podcast.”

#1841. Manchester United: Why Patrick Dorgu equaliser vs Aston Villa stood as Old Trafford theory emerges

Manchester United benefited from home advantage regarding their controversial late equaliser against Aston Villa.

That is according to Sky Sports pundit Tim Sherwood, with the ex-Villa head coach claiming that the potential foul in the goal is never given ‘in the 96th minute at Old Trafford’.

Man United twice rallied back from two goals behind to record a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, with their last two goals scored in second half injury time.

Goalkeeper Senne Lammens went up for a corner with United trailing, and while he did not get on the end of the cross, fans on social media believed he body-checked opposite number Zion Suzuki, preventing the Villa goalkeeper from claiming the ball.

Instead, substitute Patrick Dorgu sparked wild celebrations by heading home and levelling scores.

During Sky Sports’ Ref Watch segment, former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believed the decision to be correct.

Gallagher shared: “I think it is a goal - does he make a lot of contact? He does make contact, there is no doubt about that.

“Is Suzuki strong enough? I am not sure, we saw last week against Fulham a similar incident where he goes to punch the ball. He goes into an area that is congested and once he gets there, he needs to get a firm punch on it and he does not.

“There is minimal contact, although there is contact, there is no doubt about that. Lammens is not looking at the ball and that does go against him, but is he looking to find a space, so it is harder for the goalkeeper to come through?

“It is one where the referee makes the decision and we talk about VAR assisting the referee, it has to be about the referee, who says 'no' and I think the referee is right.”

But fellow pundit Sherwood was not in agreement, pointing out that Matheus Cunha also impacted Suzuki’s ability to play the ball.

Sherwood added: “I think it is a foul, but do you get it in the 96th minute at Old Trafford? No.

“Is Lammens looking at the ball? No. He is a goalkeeper and knows how much contact he needs to give Suzuki there.

“The main offender was Cunha, who grabs Suzuki's left arm, which is what stops him.”

Jay Bothroyd agreed with Sherwood, stating: “I do think Suzuki needs to be better, he needs to be stronger and get a punch away.

“Lammens clearly does not have his eyes on the ball, he is going into the 'keeper to put him off and there was some contact there when he went into him.

“If they had blown up for that, I would have known why. I think it is a foul as he is not looking at the ball and has gone into the 'keeper.”

#1840. Arsenal boost after shock Noni Madueke snub as training plan revealed for new undroppable

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

When Thomas Tuchel named his latest England squad last week, the core that has been established at Arsenal was evident.

The Gunners had five players included for upcoming Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain. It is not just more than any other club, but more than the other five of the traditional ‘Big Six’ combined.

That is despite Bukayo Saka not being involved due to the quad injury he suffered against Bayern Munich last month.

Even with such strong representation, it was an Arsenal player not included in Tuchel’s squad who attracted the most attention.

Noni Madueke can feel incredibly hard done by to miss out on a return to the England setup.

He has stepped up significantly since the last international break and filled the void left by Saka in the Arsenal side as well as, or perhaps even better than, anyone could have expected.

The winger has three goals and an assist in his last nine appearances, eight of which have been starts. It is the best run of consistent minutes of his Arsenal career.

As unfortunate as he has been to not make the cut for England, Madueke’s exclusion should be to Arsenal’s benefit.

It is understood that Madueke will be flying abroad during this international break for some warm-weather training - something Mikel Arteta has happily signed off on.

The winger is viewing it as a period to build on his best run in an Arsenal shirt and he is determined to maintain the sharpness and intensity that has impressed Arteta in recent weeks.

The plan is for Madueke to then return to Arsenal’s training ground at London Colney towards the start of next week to begin preparations for Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle.

It is a formula that has worked well for Madueke and Arteta is keen for it to be replicated.

The last international break, when the 24-year-old was also not called up by Tuchel, was something of a turning point for Madueke.

Up to that stage in the season, he had played just 23 minutes of Premier League football. Madueke was very much on the periphery of Arteta’s thinking.

One of the few first-team players not called up by their country, the extended three-week break offered Madueke the chance to switch off from football if he wanted to.

Instead, he flew to Portugal, not for a holiday but to train in the sun. Madueke asked for an individual training programme, determined to build his sharpness and prove a point to Arteta and Tuchel. He trained hard through the international break.

When Madueke then returned to Arsenal’s training ground, Arteta and his coaching staff were convinced they had a “different Noni” in front of them. Madueke’s commitment during that time in Portugal made a real impression on Arteta.

Even as the full squad gradually returned from international duty, it was still Madueke catching Arteta’s eye.

Arteta had been frustrated with Madueke earlier in the season, believing he was not doing enough to merit more opportunities.

He’s been incredible... he gave me no option but to select him

Mikel Arteta on Noni Madueke’s recent form

That stance changed over the last international break. Messages that were not being taken on board sufficiently earlier in the season were now getting the response Arteta demanded.

The sense from the Arsenal manager was that Madueke could not have done more to force his way into the team and he deserved to be rewarded.

In the first match back after that international break, Madueke started ahead of Eberechi Eze on the left wing against Leeds.

“He’s been the best player in the last 10 days,” Arteta said of Madueke’s training performances. “He gave me no option not to select him and not to play him today.”

Madueke was starting to make the left wing shirt his own but Saka’s injury necessitated a switch back to the right. He has played the full 90 minutes in every Premier League and Champions League match since then.

In a short space of time, Madueke has made himself undroppable. No player in the Premier League is creating more chances per 90 minutes this season. His figure of 3.57 is more than double what he produced last term.

Against Hull on Saturday, Madueke had more touches in the opposition box than any Arsenal player has managed in the league all season.

There is a relentlessness to the way Madueke attacks. He does not stop running at his man.

In the past, too much of that has felt chaotic, relying on high volume to cover for a lack of efficiency. Increasingly, Madueke is delivering the end product that has been the missing piece of his game.

Speaking after the Hull match, Arteta laid down the challenge to Madueke. Now he has had a “different Noni” at his disposal, Arteta wants even more.

“He’s been incredible,” the Arsenal manager said. “Now you are in that position, now you need to hold it and improve it, and he can still do that. So let’s see what he does in this break.”

#1839. Now will the FA put their money where their mouth is? England chiefs and UEFA must decide whether to back rival Japanese bid to FIFA president Gianni Infantino after slamming World Cup controversial sell-off plan

Published: 08:23 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 11:00 EST, 5 November 2026

The FA and UEFA face a dilemma over whether to support a bid to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency after honorary Japanese FA president Kohzo Tashima announced his decision to stand.

Alongside the FA, UEFA have spearheaded opposition to Infantino following the collapse of his botched deal to sell stakes in the World Cup.

However, despite declaring Infantino 'has lost the confidence of UEFA' and threatening to boycott the World Cup, the European governing body have so far failed to come up with a candidate to challenge him at the March election in Rabat.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin decided against a run for the FIFA presidency, opting instead to focus on securing another term at the top of European football.

At a meeting of the FA Council last month FA chair Debbie Hewitt demanded answers over the World Cup sell-off plan - and decision to suspend the ban of US striker Folarin Balogun after pressure from Donald Trump. She said: 'The man has to answer those questions, and if he doesn't answer those questions, no, he's not fit to be FIFA president, and that was what was shared in the meeting.'

But there is a growing feeling that a European candidate would struggle to secure sufficient support from the rest of the world, while Infantino believes he already has enough votes to secure re-election, making it difficult to find a credible challenger.

Japanese FA president Kohzo Tashima has announced a decision to stand for FIFA presidency

Tashima will run against the controversial current president Gianni Infantino (left)

That said, FIFA Council member and Japanese FA bigwig Tashima could split the Asian vote and is well respected in Europe.

With Tashima - the first candidate to secure the backing of a national association - declaring his intention to run, pressure is now mounting on the FA and UEFA to either support his bid or put forward a candidate of their own, having called for Infantino to step down.

It follows former Tottenham and Switzerland footballer Ramon Vega making a public leadership bid on Wednesday, though it is unclear whether he could obtain the backing of enough national associations.

Candidates require the support of five football associations to run for the presidency and must pass eligibility checks by November 18.

Tashima is the first candidate with a realistic chance to announce an intention to run before the November 18 deadline, where the support of five national associations is required.

Speaking to Japanese newspaper Sports Nippon, Tashima said: ‘I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the Japan Football Association.

‘It’s not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What FIFA needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world.’

#1838. Man United break another unwanted record vs. Aston Villa after Alysson, Nicolas Jackson goals

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 16:50, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 17:00

Manchester United have broken yet another unwanted club record after falling 2-0 down inside just four minutes against Aston Villa.

On the back of Tuesday's extraordinary 3-2 win over Roma in the Champions League, Michael Carrick could have been forgiven for expecting a fierce response domestically on Sunday afternoon.

However, the Englishman instead oversaw yet another disastrous opening, as Villa winger Alysson took just one minute to break the deadlock with a low strike through Senne Lammens's legs.

The Red Devils then found themselves two goals behind just a few moments later, as Nicolas Jackson followed in after a Lammens save to tap home the visitors' second.

Jackson's strike marked a shocking new low for Man United, who broke their record for the quickest time to fall 2-0 down in a Premier League game at three minutes and 40 seconds.

2 - After three minutes and 40 seconds, this is the earliest Manchester United have ever been 2-0 down in a Premier League game. Slumber. https://t.co/76iMwVLhTK

Boos rang out around an already febrile Old Trafford following Jackson's goal, the ground already awash with a sea of green and yellow in protest against the Glazer family's ownership of the club.

Carrick and United's players were subsequently subjected to a collection of brutal chants from the crowd, such as "you're not fit to wear the shirt" and "you're getting sacked in the morning".

Villa fans also took aim at former midfielder Youri Tielemans, chanting "you used to play for a big club" and poking fun at Bruno Fernandes's recent public criticism, bellowing out "Bruno's right, you're f****** s****".

However, Fernandes then gave Man United a sliver of hope from the penalty spot, calmly sending Zion Suzuki the wrong way after Matheus Cunha was scythed down by Boubacar Kamara.

If the Red Devils cannot fight back to beat Villa, though, they will enter the international break in 19th place in the Premier League table after Sunderland's surprise 1-0 win over Chelsea lifted the Black Cats off the bottom.

Even if Man United fell to a catastrophic loss vs. Roma in midweek, Carrick would have almost certainly taken the reins against Aston Villa, as the hierarchy always intended to get to the international break before conducting a thorough review.

The former Red Devils midfielder is still widely adored by the majority of the fanbase, whose frustrations are instead directed towards the Glazers, INEOS and the players themselves.

Man United cannot correct years of terrible transfer calls and a toxic culture overnight, but they can make a coaching change in the blink of an eye, and Carrick would undoubtedly be the fall guy if the powers-that-be decide that change if necessary.

Fernandes publicly calling out the tactics of the coaching staff hinted at discontent behind the scenes, and unless Man United pull off another fabulous fightback on Sunday, Carrick will surely be taking charge of his beloved club for the final time.

#1837. Premier League verdict may be impacting Man City results, says Neville

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Manchester City's guilty Premier League verdict is a "cloud" hanging over the club that may be impacting their recent performances, Gary Neville has hypothesised.

In late September, the Premier League confirmed City had been found guilty of all charges related to "serious breaches" of the competition's financial rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

City were also found guilty of the majority of charges relating to the club's failure to comply with the Premier League's investigation.

While City have pledged to fight that verdict, rumours have swirled regarding the possible punishments that could be handed down, with pundits and supporters suggesting huge points deductions, automatic relegations or the stripping of past titles.

Initially, Enzo Maresca's squad did not appear to be affected by the off-pitch noise, as City won seven straight Premier League games to start the campaign.

However, they have since succumbed to defeats against Aston Villa (2-1), Brighton (1-0) and Nottingham Forest (3-1).

They are just the second team in English top-flight history – after Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05 – to win their first seven games of a season before losing their next three.

And former Manchester United defender Neville has now questioned whether City's players are starting to be impacted by the speculation.

"Something's just not right at the moment and it's worrying. Things point towards the obvious cloud hanging over the club," Neville told NBC Sports' Premier League Mornings.

"Is it finally catching up with them, in terms of the mental fatigue of the negative publicity they've had, and the effect it's had on the players?

"Are they drained physically and mentally through that, or are they just going through a bad patch?

"Either way, Maresca has got to sort it out quite quickly in the international break, because that won't be tolerated. Losing games like that doesn't happen very often."

Club statement.  https://t.co/yrJ8Z0A52Y https://t.co/0NP2k33JT9

— Manchester City (@ManCity) September 29, 2026

And Neville says speculation over City being thrown out of the Premier League – and the knock-on effect such a punishment would have on their players – is bound to be a distraction.

He added: "Those players will constantly be getting asked, 'What do you think is going to happen? What happens if they do get relegated? Will you stay?'

"Now you imagine your family is having to put up with that, your agent's thinking about those things… it can't be ruled out as a factor that's going to start to seep in.

"If you lose a football match or two, you can start to look at that as an excuse, but they've got to play better, they've got to compete in games, they've got to make sure that they do better on the pitch from a tactical and physical perspective.

"But I do believe it will be having some impact, just because of the weight of what's been hitting them, from a publicity point of view."

City will spend the international break third in the Premier League, six points adrift of Arsenal and one behind Brighton, with Fulham being their next opponents on November 21.
